Employing the Hamiltonian formalism, we establish the quantum statistical relation between the Euclidean on-shell action and the Gibbs free energy. We further compute the leading four-derivative corrections to the thermodynamics of a rotating magnetic black string using the Reall-Santos method. The resulting corrections are in precise agreement with previous results obtained directly for the Kerr-Newman black hole in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity.

papers.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.

papers.title: Altermagnetism-induced higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems
papers.abstract: We propose an altermagnetism-induced route to a two-dimensional higher-order topological Dirac semimetal in a trilayer nonsymmorphic Dirac system. Interlayer hybridization preserves the nonsymmorphic bulk Dirac crossings and generates helical edge states in the trilayer phase. Introducing outer-layer $d$-wave altermagnetic order gaps the helical edge states, while only the symmetry-protected Dirac crossing at high-symmetry point $M$ remains gapless. The resulting phase hosts a surviving bulk Dirac point, gapped edge spectra, and corner states. An exact layer-space decomposition further reveals that these features arise from the coexistence of a gapless Dirac sector and a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological sector. Our results establish altermagnetism as an effective mechanism for engineering higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.

papers.title: Pairwise Distortion Distribution with Graph-Based Importance Sampling for Quantization Error and Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
papers.abstract: Quantifying the dimensionality of data is a fundamental need in machine learning and signal processing applications such as representation learning, data compression, and inverse problems, where the extrinsic dimension in which the data is presented can be very different from the intrinsic dimension that determines the operational performance. Various concepts, such as Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension are useful here. Despite their theoretical significance, estimating these measures are challenging given their asymptotic definitions. Recent research has shown that analyzing the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) of a data source can provide a tractable lower bound on the distortion of random codebook quantization, from which a tractable notion of intrinsic dimension can be derived. In this paper we extend this line of research in three main ways. First, we develop a related upper bound on distortion of random codebook quantization. Second, we improve the computability of both the lower and upper bounds, using a graph-based adaptive importance sampling approach. Third, we leverage the bounds to define new notions of intrinsic dimension which form upper and lower bounds on the Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension, and which can be empirically estimated from unknown data sources. We illustrate the concepts by analyzing several artificial and empirical distributions.

papers.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
papers.abstract: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness, in-plane homogeneous, in-plane isotropic layer with a general nonlocal susceptibility, using a single-scale asymptotic expansion in $η= l\max(k_0,q)$, where $l$ is the layer thickness, $k_0$ the free-space wavenumber and $q$ the in-plane wavenumber. The sheet limit must be taken after resumming the out-of-plane depolarizing field, as this ensures that the resulting sheet susceptibility is independent of the material thickness. The arithmetic mean then emerges as the leading-order polarizing field for general susceptibility profiles. Asymmetries in the layer profile modify the effective susceptibility appearing in the transition conditions, rather than altering the arithmetic-mean field prescription. If the spatial profile is not even in both out-of-plane coordinates, in-plane and out-of-plane response hybridize, turning the diagonal volumetric susceptibility into a $q$-dependent effective tensor surface susceptibility with off-diagonal components. Mirror symmetry alone does not remove this hybridization. Comparison with exact solutions for local and separable layers shows that the derived conditions remain accurate to $O(η)$ across propagating and evanescent excitations, whereas the standard sheet conditions fail once hybridization becomes appreciable.

papers.title: Anomalous Hall Response and Real-Space Current Correlations in Rhombohedral Graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and magnetization observed in rhombohedral graphene through real-space calculations which lead to new insights. Our calculations reveal no equilibrium loop currents of the type associated with the Haldane model of a quantum anomalous Hall insulator. Instead, the AHE arises in this instance from interference between electronic paths forming oriented closed Wilson loops of current operators in the presence of valley polarization. We show some examples of these Wilson loops. Using the fact that the added-carrier charge density resides dominantly in the top and bottom layers, we develop a real-space expansion of the surface Hamiltonian that reproduces the Hall response of the full model with good accuracy. We also predict that a smooth local potential induces equilibrium circulating currents whose strength depends on both Berry curvature and the orbital moments of states at the Fermi surface.

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

papers.title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
papers.abstract: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.

papers.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
papers.abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,α),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,α)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.

papers.title: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation
papers.abstract: Histogram estimation is a fundamental primitive in distributed data analysis, with applications in counting queries and federated learning. In many settings, the universe of categories is enormous, yet each user's data involves only a small subset, yielding sparse local histograms. This raises a natural question: To what extent can local sparsity reduce the communication needed to estimate the global histogram? We answer this question by characterizing the communication complexity of distributed sparse histogram estimation under prescribed $\ell_1$ distortion and failure probability constraints. Our upper bound is achieved by a randomized covering scheme that optimizes how accurately each user represents its local histogram to reduce communication. By exploiting the distortion budget directly rather than imposing unbiasedness, the scheme achieves lower communication costs than standard unbiased sampling and hashing constructions. We establish the scheme's first-order optimality through a lower bound based on local support identification. The key step is to relate communication cost directly to the number of active coordinates revealed by each user's message, rather than to bound information about the aggregate via distance-based Fano's inequalities. This characterization further quantifies how the communication advantage of heterogeneous over homogeneous encoders varies across parameter regimes.

papers.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them. We formulate proof rules for establishing the correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove their soundness with respect to the proposed semantic model.

papers.title: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier results for closed quantum systems, we investigate the dynamical evolution of quantum fluctuations and their connections to Fisher information and the quantum operations describing open-system dynamics. Starting from a general expression for the time derivative of an observable's uncertainty, we derive an alternative upper bound on fluctuation growth in an open quantum system using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The resulting bound separates contributions from the evolution of the quantum state and the explicit time dependence of the observable, reducing to a known result for closed-system dynamics. We then establish a connection between fluctuation dynamics and quantum Fisher information by decomposing the density operator and the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) into coherent and incoherent contributions, which leads to a bound relating the evolution of observable uncertainty to the coherent and incoherent components of the Fisher information, providing an information-geometric interpretation of fluctuation growth. To connect fluctuation dynamics with quantum operations governing open-system evolutions, we derive the time evolution of the eigenvalues of the density operator in terms of Kraus operators. Using the infinitesimal-time relation between Kraus and Lindblad operators, we obtain a corresponding expression for the eigenvalue dynamics in terms of Lindblad operators. This formulation directly relates changes in the density operator eigenvalues to the quantum processes acting on the system. We then study the results using some examples. Our results provide a framework connecting observable fluctuation growth, Fisher information, and the Kraus and Lindblad descriptions of quantum evolution, offering a route toward understanding how specific quantum channels influence the information and fluctuations available in an evolving quantum system.

papers.title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.

papers.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
papers.abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.

papers.title: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement
papers.abstract: A three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in $2+1$ dimensions yields a strictly negative logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for every integer $n\geq3$ and all nondegenerate sector angles. The replica subtraction exactly removes loop classes associated with a single interface. Surviving loops have positive, scale-independent weight, yielding a logarithm whose sign is fixed by the negative Rényi prefactor. The selector is empty at $n=2$. The flat-sheet Friedrichs prescription fixes the scalar operator at the nonmanifold replica apex. It yields a convergent angular spectral formula for the coefficient.

papers.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
papers.abstract: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling for Quantum LDPC Decoders
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their decoding algorithms present significant hardware implementation challenges. Reinforcement-learned sequential belief propagation (RL-S) improves the error-correction performance of conventional belief propagation (BP) through adaptive variable-node scheduling. However, its heap-based priority management introduces substantial hardware overhead. This paper presents hardware implementations of BP, RL-S, and bucket-based reinforcement-learned BP (BRL-S) for the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle QLDPC code. The BRL-S architectures employ quantized priorities and first-in, first-out (FIFO) buckets to simplify scheduling. Three configurations with two, four, and eight priority levels are evaluated. FPGA synthesis results demonstrate that BRL-S reduces lookup-table utilization by approximately 68--72% compared with RL-S. ASIC synthesis further shows reductions of 63--67% in area and 64--69% in estimated power consumption. These results demonstrate that bucket-based scheduling substantially improves the hardware efficiency of reinforcement-learned QLDPC decoders.

papers.title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
papers.abstract: Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.

papers.title: Quantum identity authentication protocol via perturbed probability amplitudes
papers.abstract: Quantum identity authentication is an effective solution for establishing mutual trust between communicating parties in the post-quantum era. To address the risk of partial secret information leakage under special measurements, this paper designs a quantum identity authentication protocol based on perturbed probability amplitudes. The protocol first proposes a method of encoding a random sequence onto the probability amplitudes of quantum entangled states, forming perturbed probability amplitudes, thereby reducing the involvement of shared information between the sender and receiver. Furthermore, it presents a method for generating n-bit random authentication information based on the n-bit pre-shared information, enhancing the randomness of the authentication information relative to an attacker. The proposed protocol can resist impersonation attack, CNOT attack, and entanglement measurement attack, and ensures backward security. Under equivalent security conditions, the amount of shared information is 1/n that in Chen et al.'s scheme and half that in Dutta et al.'s scheme. And each bit of the secret message has no risk of leakage under special measurements. It can also be extended to a bi-directional quantum identity authentication protocol.

papers.title: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.abstract: Jointly supporting communication and distributed sensing over a shared, limited pool of entanglement resources is an attractive prospect for future quantum networks. We develop a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates elementary Bell pairs between communication users and distributed sensing. Sensing resources are adaptively partitioned among multiple GHZ probes with dynamically selected sizes and sensing-node assignments. We derive an effective quantum Fisher information model accounting for probabilistic fusion, transmission loss, and memory decoherence, and formulate a finite-horizon allocation problem subject to communication QoS, expected sensing-information, sensing-reliability, and hardware constraints. A hierarchical constrained proximal policy optimization (HC-PPO) framework combines learned discrete sensing allocation with analytical continuous communication allocation. Numerical results show that GHZ probing requires approximately $27$--30% fewer sensing qubits than separable probing under modest probe-size caps and 65-67% fewer at the highest considered target under the same sensing requirements. Adaptive multi-GHZ partitioning provides greater robustness than single-GHZ sensing, while adaptive communication--sensing sharing outperforms the evaluated fixed splits. The proposed HC-PPO framework satisfies the joint requirements in at least 99.9% of test instances across the considered sensing targets and fusion probabilities. Monte Carlo evaluation separately shows that realized terminal information reached its target in 96-98% of realizations, distinguishing expected-information satisfaction from realized sensing performance.

papers.title: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels
papers.abstract: We study single-query perfect anti-distinguishability/exclusion tasks of finite quantum channel ensembles, primarily using associated Choi operators and process POVMs. Weak perfect anti-distinguishability requires each measurement outcome to exclude an ensemble candidate with certainty, whereas the strong form additionally requires every candidate to have an exclusion outcome occurring with non-zero probability. For pairs of channels, both coincide with perfect distinguishability, whereas larger ensembles exhibit separations. We derive Choi-operator-support-based obstructions: weak exclusion requires at least two rank-deficient Choi operators, while strong exclusion requires the support of every candidate Choi operator to be strictly contained in the joint Choi support. The common Choi support must also lie in the kernel of the PPOVM normalisation. For commuting Choi operators, this condition is sufficient for weak exclusion when the normalisation also commutes with them. Conversely, a nonzero admixture of the same noise channel into every candidate precludes weak exclusion for any probe. We apply these results to measure-and-prepare, state-space contraction, Pauli, and replacer channels. In particular, the full permutation-channel ensemble of an unlabeled POVM is strongly anti-distinguishable exactly when some POVM effect is rank-deficient, while replacer-channel exclusion reduces to state exclusion. A Choi-commuting ensemble exhibits strong exclusion with an unassisted probe although no positive-definite PPOVM normalisation permits even weak exclusion. In contrast, commuting qubit phase gates, whose Choi operators need not commute, admit exact convex-hull criteria for weak and strong exclusion, both attainable without assistance.

papers.title: Chirality rules for optical vortices in rhombohedral graphene multilayers
papers.abstract: Optical zeros are momenta where the interband dipole vanishes. The dipole phase winds around each of them by an integer, so they are vortices of the resonant optical response with a conserved charge. We show that in rhombohedral graphene multilayers one integer, the stacking chirality $N$, fixes their constellation near the $K$ valley: the total charge per linear polarization is $N-1$ and is conserved under trigonal warping and interlayer bias; for $N\ge3$ the $K$ point stays an exact optical zero, the Bernal bilayer being the only exception; warping places the remaining charge on satellites whose radii scale linearly with the warping; and the charge pinned at $K$ is bias independent for $N\ge4$. A quantized interband character counts the enclosed charge as an integer staircase with steps at these radii, and an interlayer bias drives a satellite through the protected $K$ vortex in the trilayer. The rules survive the remote hoppings of the full tight-binding model and, being integer charges, the corrections that reshape the bands. The same integer sets the magnitude of the response: the band-edge shift current grows linearly with $N$.

papers.title: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled $R_z$ Synthesis
papers.abstract: In Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) using surface codes, reducing $T$-count is critical for efficient computation due to the high cost of $T$-state distillation. Probabilistic Quantum Circuit with Fallback (PQF) synthesis significantly lowers $T$-counts compared to standard protocols like Gridsynth, but introduces high circuit dynamism through extra gates inserted at runtime. This dynamism invalidates static compile-time routing, as these new $T$ gates require dynamic lattice surgery routing to establish non-intersecting ancilla paths to $T$-state factories while minimizing total execution time. To address this, we introduce $\text{R}^2$-PQF, a Runtime Routing protocol for PQF-synthesized quantum circuits. $\text{R}^2$-PQF dynamically routes gates layer-by-layer, computing paths during the execution of the previous logical timestep. To satisfy the strict computational window of $\sim t_{lattice\_surgery} + t_{reaction}$ and non-intersectionality constraints, we implement a Wavefront Breadth-First Search (W-BFS) and synthesise it on a 500MHz FPGA and 2 GHz ASIC. For a clock cycle of 2GHz, we achieve a median logical time-step of $1.51 μs$ for a 300 qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, demonstrating that $\text{R}^2$-PQF successfully resolves the vast majority of paths (with rare exceptions) within the execution window and enables the $T$-count benefits of PQF without latency penalties. Compared to a baseline stalling-based solution (the only no-runtime-recomputation solution), $\text{R}^2$-PQF speeds up circuit execution by $1.34\times$ on average and up to $1.76 \times$.

papers.title: Continuum Dirac Theory and Nonlinear Extensions of a Chain of Alternating non-linear springs: an SSH version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model
papers.abstract: A mechanical version of the SSH model, made of equal masses joined by two alternating non-linear springs is studied in the continuum limit. Such a non-linear dimerized mechanical chain generates a nonlinear, dispersive, two-field hyperbolic system of Boussinesq type of differential equations, describing coupled acoustic and gapped optical fields. The corresponding Lagrangian density is found, revealing that the acoustic and optical degrees of freedom are coupled through a structure that is formally analogous to a synthetic spin-orbit coupling, where the spatial motion is locked to the internal sublattice degree of freedom. An emergent non-Abelian Berry connection term also appears. Some particular solitary-wave solutions are found using variational theory, as the effective optical field obeys an undamped and unforced cubic-quintic Duffing equation. Near the Brillouin-zone edge, the system becomes a nonlinear Dirac field theory of the Soler type, providing a direct mechanical realization of interacting relativistic solitons. By factoring out fast spatial oscillations, an effective Jackiw-Rebbi Hamiltonian is obtained, with topological zero modes at domain walls. These modes are akin to the electronic flat bands in moire graphene systems associated with superconductivity and charge fractionalization. Finally, we discuss the mechanical rigidity transition and its effects on the fields as the system evolves toward the fully dimerized limit, in which the zero modes are floppy modes.

papers.title: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link in which a low-power transmitter simultaneously communicates with a receiver and identifies the range of a defect producing a backscattered signal. We model the system as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, in which the target, modeled as a beamsplitter, affects the timing of the backscattered signal through its location. Motivated by the envisioned deployment of entanglement-enabled quantum networks, we develop two protocols that allow the transmitter to leverage shared Gaussian entanglement, in the form of independent two-mode squeezed vacuum states or coupled three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. Since entanglement is known to enhance sensing, as demonstrated in quantum illumination, and to increase communication rates through entanglement-assisted communication, the transmitter faces a trade-off in allocating its entanglement resources between the two tasks. Our main results characterize these trade-offs under the proposed protocols in terms of achievable communication rate/sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

papers.title: Energy-Resolved Cross-Correlation of THz Field Emission of Electrons from a Metal Nanotip
papers.abstract: Intense THz pulses, combined with the lightning-rod field enhancement at metal nanotips, can drive field emission of keV-energy, femtosecond-duration electron bunches, yet the dynamics governing this emission remain largely unexplored. Here we probe these dynamics by cross-correlating the energy-resolved emission driven by two independently generated single-cycle THz pulses focused onto a tungsten nanotip, scanning their relative delay over 160 ps. At total bunch charges approaching $10^6$ e$^-$, the delay-energy emission map near zero delay reveals electrons accelerated up to 2.1 keV, with a cross-correlation width of ~210 fs full width at half maximum at the highest energies. Apart from replicas caused by optical reflections in the setup, no emission echoes are observed over the full delay range, ruling out long-lived antenna resonances such as Sommerfeld-wave reflections along the tip shaft. A 1D Fowler-Nordheim model incorporating a low-$Q$, sub-picosecond antenna response for the local field enhancement reproduces the peak electron energies and the asymmetry of the delay-energy map. Our results indicate that each THz pulse produces a single, isolated electron burst, and that energy filtering can select its shortest, highest-energy component.

papers.title: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
papers.abstract: We construct binary codes that attain the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors, with deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding. For every fixed integer $t\ge 1$ and all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, our codes correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions in total, with redundancy at most $2t\log_2 n+O_t(1)$. All algorithms run in polynomial time in $n$ for fixed $t$, and decoding recovers the original information message. This realizes the classical counting guarantee algorithmically without enumerating the exponentially large space of binary words.

papers.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme to realize Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial bands in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Spin-flip hopping suppressed by the large Zeeman detuning is resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, yielding a correlated spin-orbit coupling that depends on the local particle configuration. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold $^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results highlight density-assisted spin-orbit coupling as a mechanism for realizing Weyl superfluidity in strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: Tight Quasiprobabilistic Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Discrete Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: It was conjectured by Wehrl and proven by Lieb that the Shannon differential entropy of the Husimi function of a continuous-variable quantum state is lower bounded by the value it takes on coherent states. This corroborates the intuition, familiar from Heisenberg's uncertainty relations, that coherent states are minimal uncertainty states. The analogous statement for the Wigner function would be that the Wigner differential entropy of states with a positive Wigner function is bounded below by the entropy of pure Gaussian states. This was conjectured a decade ago, but recently disproven. Here, we prove the analogous statement for Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with mutually unbiased bases and for the Gross-Wigner distributions. For these discrete systems, the entropy-minimizing role is played by the pure states with positive quasiprobability distributions. Further, we prove that Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with large nonpositivity have large uncertainty.

papers.title: Reconfigurable multi-tone mmWave/THz generation powered by high-efficiency Kerr parametric oscillation
papers.abstract: Broadband and simultaneously accessible multi-tone millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) signals are attractive for multi-band wireless communication and spectroscopy applications, yet their generation remains constrained by electronic bandwidth limitations and inefficient optical frequency conversion. Here, we demonstrate reconfigurable photonic generation of multi-tone mmWave/THz signals with comb spacings of 100, 200, 300, and 400 GHz, using a strongly asymmetric dual-ring silicon-nitride (SiN) microresonator and a broadband spiral plasmonic photomixer. A localized avoided-mode crossing (AMX) introduced by an auxiliary ring supports a fixed optical parametric oscillation (OPO) mode pair over an extended pump-detuning range, consistent with passive compensation of detuning-dependent phase mismatch. This enables a maximum pump-to-generated-line conversion efficiency of 67.3 % with 25.06 dB of pump depletion across different pump wavelength selections. Direct photomixing of these optical states produces simultaneous multi-frequency tones spanning 100 to 900 GHz without intermediate optical amplification. The generated carriers are further characterized through down-converted spectra, frequency-noise power spectral density (PSD), and Allan deviation measurements, yielding a \b{eta}-separation linewidth of 26 kHz at an observation time of 0.1 s. Optical modulation offers high radiated power levels exceeding 2 mW at 100 GHz at a duty cycle of 1 %, while mitigating thermal breakdown in the photomixer. High optical conversion efficiency, reconfigurable and selectable comb spacings, and broadband multi-tone generation on a chip-scale platform provide a compact route toward reconfigurable multi-band mmWave/THz sources for wireless communication, spectroscopy, and sensing.

papers.title: Adaptive Qubit Encoding for Continuous-Variable Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: Optimizing continuous-variable functions on qubit-based quantum hardware requires a finite representation of the search space and a solver-compatible representation of the objective function. Fixed-grid discretizations provide a direct encoding, but restrict the search to a predefined range and resolution; at the same time, constructing a compact Hamiltonian for a general continuous-variable objective can be impractical. Here, we introduce a framework for continuous-variable optimization tailored to qubit-based quantum architectures. The method combines an adaptive discretization with an iterative local mapping of the objective function onto an effective spin-glass Hamiltonian. We assess the approach on unconstrained and constrained instances of the $n$-dimensional Gramacy-Lee benchmark, and on a proof-of-concept inverse-planning problem in intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) for cancer treatment. The results show that this framework can produce competitive solutions, supporting its use as a flexible mapping strategy for continuous-variable optimization in qubit-based quantum and quantum-inspired pipelines.

papers.title: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spin ensembles are a promising platform for accurate vector magnetometry, as they offer measurements referenced to a spin Hamiltonian in an anisotropic crystal with native vector sensing capabilities. However, charged dopants within the diamond produce random internal electric fields (RIEFs) that shift NV spin-transition frequencies, and their impact on the accuracy of NV magnetometry has not been investigated. Here, we characterize RIEFs' effect on NV spin-transition spectra and propose an analytical fitting function to improve accuracy in their presence. We build a Monte Carlo RIEF model that reproduces the asymmetric lineshapes observed in experimental optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra, and use it as a testbed to quantify RIEF-induced errors by simulating ODMR spectra including RIEFs and comparing reconstructed magnetic fields to the known model input. With standard analysis approaches, we observe systematic errors exceeding the g-factor uncertainty in fields below $\sim$ 5 mT, while the proposed fitting function reduces the error by nearly an order of magnitude. Our results demonstrate that RIEFs can play a significant role in the systematic error budget for NV magnetometry, and offer a path towards improved accuracy in NV quantum sensing.

papers.title: On the optimality of truncation among binary linear sketches
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference and function evaluation problems in which the input binary vector is available only through a binary linear sketch, i.e., a fixed number of parity measurements. We show that under a certain monotonicity condition, simply truncating the input by retaining a subset of its coordinates is optimal among all linear sketches of the same size. In particular, this applies to distributed testing of correlations of binary vectors when they are of opposite signs and evaluating unate Boolean functions on uniformly random inputs. Additionally, given that truncation is optimal, we immediately have lower bounds for arbitrary binary linear sketches. To illustrate this application, we consider the one-way communication complexity of a distributional graph connectivity problem on $n$ vertices and show that truncation, and hence all binary linear sketches, requires $Θ(n \log n)$ bits to achieve constant error, while a nonlinear protocol only requires $O(\log n)$ bits.

papers.title: Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$_3$ via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.

papers.title: A Ghost-Free dS/AdS Correspondence in $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity
papers.abstract: Reversing the sign of the scalar potential exchanges de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua and, through the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence, maps flat domain walls onto flat FLRW cosmologies, but its supersymmetric version has ghosts on the cosmological side. We show that this pointwise correspondence is realized between two ordinary, ghost-free four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravities with spontaneously broken supersymmetry. Within a single superconformal Kähler cone, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ reflection of the nilpotent goldstino Kähler metric through the flat limit $V=0$ reverses $V\leftrightarrow-V$ pointwise while preserving the visible Kähler metric, the superpotential, and the unitary-gauge fermion Lagrangian. The paired vacua obey a sharp dictionary with $H=1/L$, $m^2_{\rm dS}=-m^2_{\rm AdS}$, equal conformal weights, and $m_{3/2}>H$, and are simultaneously stable precisely within the window $0\le m^2_{\rm dS}\le\frac94H^2$ set by the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Applied to string compactifications and cosmology, this correspondence pairs over-uplifted with under-uplifted anti-D3-brane vacua, confines the de Sitter swampland conjecture to the goldstino (anti-brane) sector, and maps slow-roll inflation onto a healthy AdS domain wall obeying the holographic $c$-theorem.

papers.title: Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the SU($N$) Thirring model at large $N$
papers.abstract: We investigate a Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Thirring model at leading order in $1/N$. We impose $f(\slashed{\partial})^\ddagger=f(\slashed{\partial})$ directly on the original action; for real nonlocality scale the admissible exponential choice is $f(\slashed{\partial})=\exp[-i\slashed{\partial}/Λ]$. We construct and analyze the even-in-mass (paired) large-$N$ effective potential and derive its radial kernel, weak-coupling dimensional-transmutation scale, and formal Lambert-$W$ zeros. Its radial gap integral possesses a conditionally convergent infinite-cutoff limit. The pairing prescription, however, differs from the unpaired determinant of the original Hermitian action, so the reported gap and spectral zeros must be understood as properties of this explicitly defined mean-field functional. We identify the further derivation needed to obtain physical mass gaps and fermion poles from the unpaired theory.

papers.title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

papers.title: Parametrization of unitary matrices, parametrizing the symmetric $S$ matrix and the $NN$ $S$ matrix above the inelastic threshold
papers.abstract: None of the $S$-matrix representations used in analyses of nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) scattering above the inelastic threshold is implicitly unitary, general, and connected to low-energy (Stapp) parameters, and hence correspondingly related to the physical properties of the scattering. Such a representation is also needed to solve the corresponding inverse scattering problem. I present an $S$-matrix representation which satisfies these requirements. As a by-product, I derive a parametrization of an $n$-dimensional unitary matrix.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moiré Flatband Superlattices
papers.abstract: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moiré superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moiré modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moiré superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moiré superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

papers.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
papers.abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(χ^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Hamiltonian of open string field theory for time-dependent solutions
papers.abstract: Using the recently introduced expression for conserved charges of $L_\infty$ theories, we give an explicit form for the Hamiltonian of Witten's bosonic open string field theory. We evaluate it on the Erler-Maccaferri analytic solution, describing any D$p$-brane configuration associated to a BCFT. We use the expression to compute the energy of the rolling tachyon solution and find exact agreement with the boundary state result by Sen.

papers.title: Ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous medium: the optical Magnus effect from Maxwell's equations
papers.abstract: We derive the ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous, isotropic and lossless medium, including the first correction to geometrical optics, the optical Magnus (spin Hall) effect. Starting from Maxwell's equations and the eikonal expansion to first order in $1/k_0$, we show that the polarization is parallel transported along the ray, identify the Berry connection and curvature of the helicity states, and obtain a ray action in which the Berry phase appears as a correction to the optical path length. This action leads to a Hamiltonian in which the refractive index is evaluated at a position shifted by the Berry connection, $\mathcal H_σ(\mathbf r,\mathbf p)=|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r+\mathbf A_σ(\mathbf p)/k_0) \simeq|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r)-k_0^{-1}\boldsymbol\nabla n\cdot\mathbf A_σ(\mathbf p)$. In terms of the physical position, the equations of motion contain the Berry curvature as an anomalous velocity. We give the equivalent non-canonical bracket form, the gauge transformation, and the equivalent time-parametrized formulation with the Hamiltonian $\hbarω=\hbar c|\mathbf k|/n$, and we state the approximations involved. The resulting ray equations are compared with analytic and numerical results. A planar interface, the helical ray in a cylindrical medium and the exact conservation of angular momentum provide checks. The formulation is set up for numerical propagation of rays in a medium with a spatially varying refractive index.

papers.title: Binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We study fully non-linear binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity with a linear Gauss-Bonnet coupling function. In the absence of a well-developed initial data solver for EsGB gravity, we demonstrate that the conventional workaround solution for massless scalar fields results in confined junk radiation that contaminates late-time dynamics in the massive theory. We propose a solution to this problem by suitably modifying the equations of motion at the early stages of the simulation to tame such junk radiation, thereby allowing us to study the dynamics of the scalar field during the process of a black hole merger. This is followed by a preliminary analysis of the frequency content in the ringdown of the scalar and tensor modes. In particular, the quadrupole scalar mode exhibits a rich ringdown structure: while it is dominated by the spin-2 ``contamination'' frequency in the early stages, its late time morphology becomes primarily determined by the scalar mass frequency.

papers.title: Non-Hermitian effective dynamics from post-selection protocols
papers.abstract: Multiple seemingly distinct frameworks are commonly proposed to explain the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems coupled to an environment. Furthermore, it remains contested how to properly calculate expectation values or whether thermal equilibrium states exist in non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we show that Feshbach projection, the Lindblad master equation, and the ancilla approach can all be understood through the Kraus map formalism, leading to non-Hermitian time evolution if an appropriate post-selection procedure is enforced. After first deriving an exact expression for the conditional system dynamics, we discuss the approximations employed in each approach and the classes of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians that can be obtained. Within this framework, we physically justify the consistency of the right-right formalism (as opposed to the biorthogonal one) for calculating expectation values. Finally, we demonstrate that the traditional notion of thermodynamic equilibrium is not applicable to general non-Hermitian systems. Consequently, stationary states are characterized as non-equilibrium steady states, which should not be conflated with system-projected thermal states of the system-environment composite.

papers.title: Analog quantum simulation of paraparticle statistics
papers.abstract: Bosonic and fermionic quantum statistics describe all known elementary and emergent particles in three dimensions, although many attempts have been made to discover other valid quantum statistical frameworks. One recent formulation proposes "$R$-paraparticles," indistinguishable particles with nonlocal internal degrees of freedom governed by generalized exchange rules [Wang and Hazzard, Nature 637, 314 (2025)]. Here, we emulate a species of paraparticle that exhibits a generalized Pauli exclusion principle using a superconducting qubit lattice. We confirm its unique quantum statistics by measuring a $180^\circ$ phase shift under paraparticle exchange, observing antibunching independent of internal degrees of freedom under two-particle interference at a beamsplitter, and finding a thermal occupation inconsistent with both Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics. These results demonstrate that parastatistics are observable on quantum simulation platforms, further motivating their use to explore theorized new phases of matter.

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes of Covariant Loop Quantum Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) and time-domain response of a massless, minimally coupled test scalar field on static, spherically symmetric covariant loop quantum black hole (cLQBH) backgrounds. Focusing on a phenomenological, Gaussian-localized holonomy profile, we obtain a localized deformation of the scalar effective potential containing both positive and negative parts. This provides a geometric realization of the bump effect, with the potential deformation and tortoise-coordinate mapping determined consistently by the same background. We characterize the deformation by its location, amplitude, and width, and study its effects using frequency-domain shooting and time-domain evolution, supplemented by matrix-pencil mode extraction and waveform reconstruction. The QNM spectrum exhibits spiral trajectories as the bump location varies, enhanced sensitivity of the overtones, and mode overtaking, whereby the branch continued from the first Schwarzschild overtone becomes longer-lived than the continued fundamental branch. Despite substantial spectral changes, the early response can remain close to its Schwarzschild counterpart, with more pronounced differences emerging later. To quantify this behavior, we introduce a local waveform-deviation time and compare it with a relative-amplitude faintness time, thereby defining an operational observation window. The deviation time depends nonmonotonically on the bump location, and suitable parameter choices allow appreciable departures to emerge before the adopted faintness threshold is reached. These results connect localized holonomy corrections with spectral sensitivity and waveform evolution, providing a basis for future gravitational-perturbation studies and assessments of gravitational-wave detectability.

papers.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast shift, which a short hardware probe on training inputs detected before the test runs. Longer replay windows raised circuit cost without a consistent gain in forecasting accuracy or hardware transfer. Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent.

papers.title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
papers.abstract: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.

papers.title: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy
papers.abstract: The Kramers theorem generally guarantees the spectral degeneracy of time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operators with half-integer spin, underlying a variety of physical phenomena. Despite its fundamental significance, the Kramers degeneracy has been argued to be absent in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states because of the double structure of the Hilbert space. Here, we instead demonstrate that the interplay of time-reversal symmetry$^†$ and parity symmetry enforces the Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillians. We explicitly construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins exhibiting the Kramers degeneracy and show that their complex spectral statistics follow those of non-Hermitian random matrices in the corresponding symplectic symmetry classes. Of the three fundamental universality classes of non-Hermitian random matrices, the symplectic class has never been realized in symmetry-resolved many-body Liouvillians. Our constructions provide its explicit realizations and spectral signatures of nonintegrability in symplectic open quantum systems.

papers.title: Exotic Pauli spinors and magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring
papers.abstract: We develop the formalism of the exotic Pauli equation and establish an effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors to describe magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring within the nonrelativistic framework. We show that, once the signs of the spatial and temporal topological terms are fixed consistently by the covariant exotic Dirac equation, this symmetry is exact at the level of the equations of motion, Lagrangians and currents, with no truncation of the exotic term and no condition on the time dependence of the topological phase. Upon deriving the flux quantization condition, we explicitly construct the composite matter-gauge unitary operator acting on the Hilbert space, which implements the symmetry at the quantum level (the gauge sector requiring the usual regularization).

papers.title: Confining strings in the reconfined phase of trace deformed three dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: Adding a trace deformation to the Yang-Mills action keeps the theory confining above the standard deconfinement temperature, in the so-called reconfined phase. We study the confining flux tube of the trace-deformed $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ theory in three dimensions with lattice simulations of Polyakov loop correlators. As the deformation increases, the ground state energy departs from the usual Nambu-Gotō effective string description, and deep in the reconfined phase the data are accurately described by the Polchinski-Yang rigid string, an effective string dominated by an extrinsic-curvature term.

papers.title: Survival-Time Risk Beyond Low-Order Channel Models: Identifiability and Scheduling
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether low-order packet-loss statistics suffice to assess survival-time risk under bursty packet losses, i.e., the probability that no update succeeds for a prescribed number of consecutive slots. Conventional models, such as the Gilbert model, characterize packet losses using the loss rate and mean burst length, but channels sharing these statistics may exhibit substantially different failure risks. We characterize the Markov channels one order above a given low-order fit that share its statistics and analyze their risks under acknowledgment-based scheduling with transmission budgets. We show that, with dense transmission attempts, risk is primarily governed by loss persistence beyond the modeled memory, and the worst-case channel need not be the most persistent one. Under limited budgets, retry spacing makes loss relapse probabilities important and can reverse the risk ordering of compatible channels. Numerical and measurement results show that low-order models can substantially underestimate the risk, highlighting the need for scheduling-dependent channel statistics.

papers.title: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format
papers.abstract: We present a preconditioning pipeline that accelerates Tensor Train (TT) linear solvers for symmetric positive-definite problems. Extending the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, we construct a preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose. This formulation is positive semidefinite for any bond dimension and truncation, and definite whenever the factor is non-singular, satisfying the mathematical requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. We detail the construction of this preconditioner and its integration into Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)-like linear solvers. Performance evaluations show consistent iteration reductions for anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems across various configurations, leading to net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned settings of time stepping schemes that can reuse the approximate inverses. These benchmarks were performed with the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl, which we also introduce in this work to provide out-of-the-box access to these preconditioned pipelines.

papers.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions. We examine how the learned control fields depend on the coupling, training configuration, and available local fields, including five exchange-type dipolar scenarios. We test the learned control fields under the Lindblad master equation with dephasing and amplitude damping, theoretically reproducing the expected first-order fidelity loss in the weak-dissipation regime. Finally, boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions represent 139 learned controls with a minimum common count of $K_\ast=24$ coefficients per control for all eleven family-averaged mean squared errors to fall below $10^{-6}$. Separately, square-pulse and Strang propagation at $K=30$ preserve all 31 continuous polynomial references within infidelity $10^{-5}$ at $N=128$ and all larger tested resolutions, under both sampling rules. These results connect multi-state gate synthesis, control-resource characterization, and compact square-pulse playback.

papers.title: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning
papers.abstract: We introduce a scalable framework for globally optimal quantum-circuit partitioning and entanglement-aware block resynthesis. The partitioning problem is formulated as an integer linear program over qubit-feasible convex subcircuits, supporting objectives such as minimizing the number of partitions or a weighted execution cost. The resulting partition selection is exact over the enumerated feasible candidates and their computed costs when the ILP is solved to proven optimality. The selected partitions are resynthesized using an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based synthesis technique, which exploits their internal entanglement structure. We compare the end-to-end integer linear programming (ILP)--OSR workflow with BQSKit while identifying their different routing methods, and separately compare local OSR and BQSKit synthesis on matched three- and four-qubit unitaries. On the frozen sample of 772 local unitary targets, OSR produces 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matches or improves the CNOT count in all 617 jointly verified pairs. These results demonstrate that globally optimal partition selection combined with entanglement-aware resynthesis improves circuit quality and extends block-based optimization to problem sizes that are impractical for existing optimization workflows.

papers.title: From off-shell strings to entropy flows
papers.abstract: Bit threads express holographic entropy as the maximal flux of a divergenceless vector field subject to a local capacity bound, but do not identify a physical carrier of that flux. In our previous work, we identified the projected string charge density with a bit-thread flow, reproduced the entropies of BTZ and ten-dimensional three-charge black holes, and showed that the maximal entropy flux is preserved under S- and T-dualities. However, the norm bound was imported from the bit-thread prescription, while the string-current configurations were prescribed along known bit-thread lines. In this paper, we give a stringy foundation for the local capacity and construct dynamical probe-string representatives of maximal flow. At genus zero and two-derivative order, the conical variation of the target-space action derived from the off-shell sphere fixes the string-frame entropy density. The gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality then yield the string-frame norm bound. We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

papers.title: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
papers.abstract: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $φ_{(1,3)}\otimes\barφ_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $η=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $β$-function. Gauging $η$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $τ_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $η$ as we lower $p$.

papers.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
papers.abstract: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

papers.title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
papers.abstract: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.

papers.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
papers.abstract: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.

papers.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
papers.abstract: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.
