We prove a nonasymptotic error bound for the Chebyshev QSD that is linear in the measurement noise, by transplanting Kirby's effective-Hamiltonian analysis to the Chebyshev--Krylov basis, and identify the block-encoding rescaling of the Hamiltonian as a parameter of the guarantee. Exact simulations of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains show that the folded reference state reduces the Krylov dimension for a given accuracy severalfold and lowers the error under noise by two to five orders of magnitude relative to the Néel state. We show how the Ritz vector is prepared as a physical state and that the ground-state generation probability obeys a tight ceiling set by the overlap, so that recursive folding prepares ground states at polynomial cost. Taken together, these results allow for a scalable QSD framework that avoids the exponentially small ground-state overlaps associated with conventional product-state initialization. Finally we compute the fold fidelity itself: a slow power law for the gapless spin-1/2 chain, a size-independent constant for the gapped spin-$1$ chain, and an exact closed form converging to 1/4 for the AKLT chain.

papers.title: Probing Coherent Noise with Stabilizer Codes: Identifiability, Ambiguity, and Decoder Priors
papers.abstract: Coherent noise calls for a reusable physical model, but Pauli twirling erases it and full process tomography scales exponentially. We turn measurement-free quantum error correction into a probe: bit-flip and phase-flip codes polarize few-qubit coherent noise into single-logical-qubit channels, and the resulting fingerprint identifies an 11-parameter three-qubit family. An exact rational-arithmetic rank certificate, evaluated at a rational point in the interior of the parameter domain, proves local injectivity on a dense open subset of that domain. The map is nevertheless not globally injective: a compensating rotation combined with a site exchange yields exact collisions, which we classify and then remove by adding one two-qubit marginal channel. The site exchange is the only nontrivial permutation symmetry of the $n$-qubit chain generator at any $n$, so the classification is structural rather than a three-qubit accident. A Cramér--Rao analysis, checked at the level of individual measurement settings, reaches $0.01$~rad per parameter at a representative point, and decoder priors rebuilt from such an estimate retain most of their correlation gain. Propagating the generator into a distance-three surface code gives a $14.8$-fold encoding gain when the generator is known exactly, and $1.21$-fold of the correlation gain survives when the prior is rebuilt from an estimate at the stated precision, closing the loop from characterization to decoding.

papers.title: Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet
papers.abstract: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.

papers.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
papers.abstract: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+ω$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.

papers.title: New analytic Janus and $S^4$ solutions for $\mathcal{N}=2^*$
papers.abstract: We construct a three-parameter family of regular analytic supergravity solutions which are dual to (a) the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ gauge theory on the four-sphere, and (b) $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$-invariant Janus interfaces in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with or without the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ mass turned on. To this end we employ a five-dimensional supergravity model coupled to six scalars which arises as a certain consistent truncation of type IIB supergravity on $S^5$. The curved domain wall solutions feature a hidden integral of motion which allows for their analytic treatment. We relate the three parameters of the solution to field theory sources and vevs and show how regularity of the solutions restricts their range. We briefly discuss the holographic evaluation of the one-point function of the field theory Lagrangian for our family of Janus solutions.

papers.title: Transport Determines Spectral Distance in Mesoscopic Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We derive a distance between thermodynamic states from a positive Hermitian transport tensor within a mesoscopic canonical model. An exact first-order factorization of the evolution generator gives a commutator norm and the metric $G=2g$, where $g$ denotes the symmetric transport tensor. Gradients of the antisymmetric tensor can change the evolution, but they leave this distance unchanged. The construction allows coordinate-dependent coefficients. For constant Onsager coefficients, a Clifford representation gives the same metric. In a two-channel thermoelectric system, the ratio of normalized principal distances is $\sqrt{1+ZT}+\sqrt{ZT}$. Transport coupling thus fixes the anisotropy of this metric. The construction requires neither an independent metric nor a physical spin variable.

papers.title: Emergent Spinorial Structure in Mesoscopic Irreversible Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Can transport coefficients determine both the coherent evolution of a mesoscopic system and distances between its thermodynamic states? We establish this connection within a canonical operator framework. Thermodynamic coordinates and conjugate forces obey commutation relations governed by a reduced constant ${\kbar}_B$. Requiring coordinate evolution to reproduce self-adjoint flux observables fixes a compatible generator up to an additive multiplication operator, set to zero in the minimal realization. The resulting equation describes coherent mesoscopic amplitudes, with transport fixing its coefficients and the reduced constant setting the evolution scale. An exact first-order factorization gives a geometry through Connes' spectral-distance prescription, including for coordinate-dependent transport. The metric is twice the inverse of the symmetric transport matrix. Coordinate derivatives of the antisymmetric part can change the dynamics without changing distances. Published thermoelectric data illustrate the geometry. A separate quadratic entropy-production observable has adjacent entropy levels separated by the reduced constant under the stated canonical and finite-mode matching assumptions. This conditional prediction offers a possible experimental signature. The evolution is unitary; irreversible relaxation requires additional mechanisms, such as environmental coupling or coarse-graining.

papers.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
papers.abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.

papers.title: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert--Varshamov Bound
papers.abstract: Correcting synchronization errors is one of the oldest problems in coding theory. In the mid-1960s, Levenshtein, and independently Ullman, showed that a single deletion can be corrected with $\log n+O(1)$ bits of redundancy, which is asymptotically optimal. For any fixed $t$, a Gilbert--Varshamov (GV) type argument shows that codes correcting $t$ deletions exist with redundancy $2t\log n+O_t(1)$. Achieving this classical GV-type bound explicitly has proved remarkably difficult. Explicit codes with redundancy $O_t(\log n)$ were first obtained by Brakensiek, Guruswami, and Zbarsky in 2016, half a century after Levenshtein, and Guruswami and Håstad matched the GV-type bound for two deletions only in 2021. For every fixed $t\ge 3$, the best explicit constructions still require roughly twice the GV-type redundancy: $(4t-1)\log n+o(\log n)$ for $t$ deletions and $4t\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ for $t$ edits (insertions, deletions, and substitutions). We close this factor-of-two gap for every fixed $t$, even in the Damerau--Levenshtein model, which also allows adjacent transpositions. We construct explicit binary codes with deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding that correct any combination of at most $t$ such errors using $2t\log n+2t\log\log n+O_t(\log\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. A single construction thus achieves the leading term of the classical GV-type bound simultaneously for deletions, edits, and Damerau--Levenshtein errors, extending the Guruswami--Håstad result from two deletions to every fixed $t$ and to substantially richer error models.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity
papers.abstract: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

papers.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
papers.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

papers.title: On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

papers.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
papers.abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.

papers.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
papers.abstract: We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI), over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$. For a polynomial $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, LLR for Shamir secret sharing asks what a few leaked bits from each of the $n$ shares $Q(α_1), \ldots, Q(α_n)$ reveal about $Q(0)$. Given (worst-case) input lists $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subset \mathbb{F}_p$, OPI seeks a polynomial $Q(X)$ so that $Q(α_i) \in S_i$ for as many $i$ as possible. Leveraging recent connections between these two problems due to (Sun, Wootters 2026), we improve the state-of-the-art for both problems. For LLR, we show that there is some constant $δ> 0$ so that Shamir secret-sharing is one-bit LLR (only a negligible amount about $Q(0)$ is learned) whenever $R := k/n \geq 1/2 - δ$. This is the first result to break the so-called ``one-half barrier'' for LLR, and improves over the previous best known result, requiring $R \geq 0.668$ (Kasser, 2025). For OPI, we give a quantum algorithm that finds a polynomial $Q(X)$ that agrees with at least a $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ(R)-\varepsilon$ fraction of the lists, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mathsf{SCL}_ρ$ is the \emph{semicircle law} of (Jordan et al., 2025). This improves previous algorithmic (and existential) results of (Jo, 2026) and (Horinaga, Yamakawa, 2026). We also give further improved existential results for all OPI instances; and when the evaluation points $α_i$ are chosen at random, for every rate $R > 0$ we show that, with high probability, for worst-case $S_i$ there exists \emph{perfect} solution. Finally, we adapt the hardness result of (Yamakawa, Zhandry, 2024) to apply to OPI (rather than a folded version); this gives an unconditional separation between the quantum and classical hardness of OPI relative to a membership oracle.

papers.title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BIC) metasurfaces are typically described by geometry-specific parameters, hindering cross-geometry comparison, while ultranarrow quasi-BIC (qBIC) features are easily diluted in full-spectrum learning. Here, we map 2,015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families onto a shared reciprocal-lattice grid. Two fixed low-order Fourier descriptors capture within-branch resonance shifts, with mean $R^2$ values of 0.871-0.999. Field-level analysis of two representative branches shows that these shifts are consistent with the Maxwell-Fourier perturbation picture. A five-channel Fourier-space backbone models the broadband spectrum. A local resonance expert uses complex Fourier coefficients to parameterize the qBIC resonance through a differentiable Fano layer. The expert reduces resonance-position mean absolute error (MAE) from 3.2 to 0.95 nm and reduces the minimum-transmission MAE by a factor of 14 on a geometry-blocked test set. The same coordinate supports spectrum-to-structure reconstruction.

papers.title: Fast holographic inversion of superconducting domes
papers.abstract: A holographic superconductor whose scalar mass depends on the gauge field strength, $M(\Fsq)$, reproduces a superconducting dome for a suitable $M$, but recovering $M$ from a dome has taken days. We obtain the condition that fixes the critical temperature from two integrations, started at the horizon and at the boundary, and its derivative with respect to $M$ from the same two solutions, so training needs no finite differences and an inversion takes ten minutes to an hour. With this speed we study the interval between the horizon value of $\Fsq$ at the lowest doping and $\Fsq=0$, which no horizon reaches and at whose end the scalar mass $M(0)$ fixes the dimension of the dual operator. Holding $M(0)$ at several values, the pinned masses, and retraining the rest, we find reconstructions that share the minima of $M$ and agree wherever the horizons reach, apart from the deepest end, but differ on that interval. A rule that keeps the reconstruction with the simplest closed form recovers the scalar mass and the mass function of a dome generated from a quadratic $M$. On Gaussian and double-Gaussian domes and the measured phase diagrams of YBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{y}$ and 2M-WS$_{2}$ its choice rests on ties or narrow margins, and it recovers the scalar mass of only two of the four domes generated from the closed forms it keeps for them. The dome thus constrains $M$ where its horizons reach but not the scalar mass, which a second observable would have to fix.

papers.title: Axial-metric/polar-gauge perturbations of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov wormhole
papers.abstract: We study linear perturbations of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov (MMP) wormhole in the parity sector pairing axial metric and polar gauge perturbations. The lowest Landau level (LLL) of the fermions responds through its charge. Its exact Schwinger current gives the longitudinal electric field the MMP screening mass $m_S^2=αq^2$, and the axial metric perturbation shifts the worldsheet gauge field of every LLL state at relative order $l(l+1)/q$. We assume that the Casimir stress tensor follows the tilting field lines. Force balance and charge conservation then fix a polarisation current, the counterpart of the polar Hall current, up to self-conserved currents. The higher Landau levels enter through the one-loop Euler-Heisenberg action, to first order in $η_{\rm H}=g_c^2/12π^2$. Virtual transitions to them could enter at the order of the $l(l+1)/q$ shift and are not estimated. At first order in the fermion backreaction $α$ the system reduces to three coupled master equations in closed form, and mouth and throat match. Consistency does not select the fermion constitutive relation. Among local closures without derivatives, covariance fixes it up to one kernel. At $α=0$ the throat has a screened, a light massive and a massless neutral channel, and the Schwinger response already breaks the isospectrality of the two parities. The higher levels raise the squared light mass by $η_{\rm H}l(l+1)$ in AdS$_2$ units and break it further. At the formal point $m_S^2=0$ the massive channels have real $O(α)$ shifts on every closed-throat level, as does the light channel at the physical $m_S^2$ on every level below the screened channel. The neutral channel has an exact zero-energy solution, a persistent current along the field lines, which the $O(α)$ mouth terms and the higher levels leave intact. Finite-element runs find no bound state below it, and its stability is open.

papers.title: Efficient detection of spectral cluster states
papers.abstract: Multimode entangled states of light are key resources for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum information processing. Exploiting their full capabilities requires detection strategies that can efficiently and simultaneously access a large number of modes and their quantum correlations. Multimode optical parametric amplification (MOPA) provides a promising approach by amplifying multiple quadratures prior to detection, rendering the measurement robust against subsequent optical losses while enabling broadband operation. Here, we demonstrate the spectral multimode capability of MOPA by simultaneously characterizing a broadband 60-node dual-rail continuous-variable cluster state. We reconstruct the cluster-state nullifiers across the spectral modes and observe nearly uniform squeezing of up to -6.9 dB, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the highest level reported for pulsed spectrally multimode squeezed light. Furthermore, by evaluating the van Loock-Furusawa criterion across all relevant bipartitions, we verify genuine multipartite entanglement throughout the 60-node state. These results establish MOPA as a promising platform for scalable high-dimensional quantum information processing in the spectral domain.

papers.title: Second-Order Image Characterization with Distortion and Secrecy
papers.abstract: Image-size characterization relates coding budgets to the probability carried by source cells and their output images. At second order, this relation must preserve the joint fluctuations of active constraints and the information available for choosing an auxiliary description. We develop simultaneous posterior and conditional-composition image bounds, together with cell-dependent reference measures for reconstruction constraints. The reference measures retain both distortion deficits in one likelihood and permit the same analytical description cost to cancel between two image comparisons. A Gaussian evaluation gives matching second-order rates for Heegard--Berger coding with one uninformed decoder in the strict both-active regime, its common-reconstruction counterpart, and the corresponding two-stage refinement corner. The framework also gives compatible helper-image intersections, reconstruction-cell bounds, and conditional-type privacy amplification. An agreed-reproduction image explains when a scalar Gaussian coefficient replaces an optimized information--distortion profile. Gaussian Wyner--Ziv and Gray--Wyner characterizations provide attributed benchmarks and complementary evaluations of the image constraints. For arbitrary helper sections, general reconstruction policies, and reliable-key generation, the finite-block bounds identify the remaining likelihood or partition constraint. The rate applications use the same observation pattern and joint performance event in the converse and construction.

papers.title: Advances in the Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence measurement using a pulsed Foil Coil
papers.abstract: In this paper, in the framework of the {\it Biréfringence Magnétique du Vide} (BMV) experiment, we present our current apparatus in detail and we discuss its critical points. We also report the results obtained using specially designed pulsed coils called Foil Coils. Our novel measurement of the vacuum linear magnetic birefringence constant is $K_{VMB} < 1.7 \cdot 10^{-21}~\text{T}^{-2}$ at a confidence level of 68$\%$, which is an improvement with respect to our previous 2014 measurement.

papers.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
papers.abstract: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model is a strongly interacting fermionic system. Its dynamics are difficult to analyze with Lieb-Robinson bounds and cluster expansions due to its all-to-all disordered interactions. We prove that, with high probability over the disorder, the SYK model admits a quantum Gibbs sampler with a system-size-independent spectral gap at sufficiently high constant temperatures. This yields polynomial-time preparation of SYK Gibbs states on a quantum computer. While prior non-rigorous computations that suggested SYK thermalization were limited to studying local correlators, we emphasize that our result holds up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance. Our proof introduces the pseudo-Lindbladian approach to fermions then applies two key new ideas: a Bochner inequality for quantum dynamics, and an especially simple SYK analysis based on a comparison to classical dynamics.

papers.title: Approximation of a continuous-variable Gaussian state by discrete-variable quantum states
papers.abstract: For every centered one-mode continuous-variable Gaussian state, we prove that the signed Wigner periodization defines a discrete-variable density operator in every odd dimension $d\ge3$. Positivity is equivalent to the one-mode uncertainty condition, and we determine the complete inertia outside and on its boundary. A covariance-independent isometric embedding gives exponential convergence in trace norm, with an explicit error bound uniform in Planck's constant. For covariance twice the identity, dimension $31$ gives a certified trace-norm error below $1/8000$. The trace-norm estimate controls all measurement probabilities. We retain the original canonical-coherent-frame formula in terms of the determinant and trace of the covariance matrix, with continuous normalization fixed to agree with the discrete frame convention. The coherence comparisons identify which diagnostics accompany the controlled state approximation. Position- and momentum-basis coherences have exponentially convergent values after division by the square root of the dimension. Numerical comparisons of purity and frame coherence illustrate the discrete-continuous transition.

papers.title: Wald entropy and Wen-Zee type gauge-curvature coupling in 2+1-dimensional gravity
papers.abstract: The Wen-Zee term is a mixed gauge-curvature coupling in the topological Chern-Simons description of a quantum Hall fluid, encoding the electric charge bound to spatial curvature. We investigate a Lorentz-covariant generalization of this coupling, expanding its scope to black-hole spacetimes and determine its contribution to horizon entropy. Such a coupling arises naturally in three-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity based on the Maxwell algebra. We show that its Wald entropy contribution is a horizon boost charge, given by a loop integral of the additional gauge field projected along the tangent to the bifurcation circle. This contribution can be nonzero even when the mixed term vanishes on shell. We show that the integral admits an Abelian holonomy interpretation when the projection direction is covariantly constant. We evaluate the charge on a flat cosmological solution and, using smooth horizon fields and a specified thermal ensemble, on an AdS-Lorentz black hole. These results connect the geometric response familiar from quantum Hall physics to gravitational horizon thermodynamics.

papers.title: Randomization Beyond Deterministic Adaptivity in Parallel Sampling
papers.abstract: Parallel samplers, including masked diffusion models, generate several coordinates per round from conditional marginals, and their accuracy depends on which coordinates are revealed together. A schedule can be improved in two natural ways: adaptively, by choosing later batches from the values already generated, or by randomization, by drawing the schedule at random. We show that randomization is strictly more powerful. For every $r \geq 1$ we construct a full-support distribution on $9r$ binary coordinates such that every deterministic three-round sampler, even with value-dependent batches and arbitrary product kernels, has forward Kullback-Leibler divergence at least $γr - \log 4$ with $γ\approx 0.0966$, whereas drawing one of four fixed schedules with two fair bits drives the divergence below $18 r β^r$ with $β\approx 0.966$. Both samplers query conditionals of the same target. The separation holds for every fixed number of rounds $T \geq 2$, a strict advantage survives perturbations of the target and errors in the conditional predictor, and exact rational arithmetic certifies the gap at nine coordinates, where trained neural predictors preserve it. The mechanism is a hidden mixture: each schedule preserves the dependence pattern of one component, while no deterministic first batch can serve them all.

papers.title: Semiclassical multi-mode squeezed states in harmonic cosmology
papers.abstract: Harmonic cosmology is an algebraic framework based on the $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ Lie algebra that underlies the effective dynamics of loop quantum cosmology and group field theory. Focusing on the multimode bosonic realization of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, we construct multimode squeezed states in harmonic cosmology and analyze their semiclassical properties by computing the relative uncertainties of the volume operator at the kinematical level. In contrast to single-mode squeezed vacua, which invariably exhibit large quantum fluctuations, we find that the relative uncertainty of the volume can be made arbitrarily small when the number of modes is large, even without displacement. Our results demonstrate that a kinematical squeezed vacuum state with a large number of independent modes can behave semiclassically providing insights into the quantum nature of bouncing cosmologies and the emergence of a classical universe.

papers.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
papers.abstract: We introduce a technique for studying state preparation complexity in the quantum $p$-spin model on $n$ qubits, a disordered quantum spin system with random interactions on every set of $p$ qubits. We reduce the task of proving state preparation lower bounds to bounding the local profile complexity of the class, a quantity derived from the metric entropy of the set of vectors recording each state's expectation values against all weight-$p$ Pauli strings. We show that, for sufficiently large fixed $p$, any class with local profile complexity $O(n^2)$ remains separated from the ground-state energy by $Ω(\sqrt n)$, a gap on the leading energy scale. When the profile complexity is $o(n^2)$, we prove the stronger conclusion that the class cannot outperform a benchmark class of simpler states at leading order. Product states always provide such a benchmark. Our framework strengthens known bounds and covers classes beyond the reach of previous methods. These include examples where circuit lightcones extend across the entire system, preventing an application of standard arguments. We obtain an $Ω(n^2/\log n)$ gate lower bound for preparing near-ground states and depth--width tradeoffs, allowing arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and arbitrarily many discardable ancillas. We also derive lower bounds on entanglement depth and matrix product state bond dimension, and energy obstructions for forward and reverse magic at every fixed level of Parham's magic hierarchy (arXiv:2504.19966). For Clifford circuits doped with $T$-gates, we obtain sharper energy comparisons using product stabilizer states as a more restrictive benchmark. The proof combines an adaptation of a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem (arXiv:1810.12197) with metric-entropy bounds for the Gaussian process indexed by the local profiles of states in the class.

papers.title: Random Quantum Circuits Beyond Moment Matching
papers.abstract: Random quantum circuits aim to efficiently reproduce the statistical properties of ideal random quantum evolution. One approach is to construct approximate unitary designs, which match the moments of Haar-random unitaries up to a prescribed order with controlled error. We establish quantitative guarantees for how accurately these designs reproduce the distribution of each output probability. We show that, for every strong $\varepsilon$-approximate unitary $k$-design on $n$ qubits, the distribution of each output probability is within $O(k^{-1/2}(1+k/2^n)^{-1/2}+\varepsilon)$ in Kolmogorov distance of the Porter-Thomas distribution, a beta distribution with parameters $1$ and $2^n-1$. This bound is optimal up to constant factors, implying that a substantially better uniform bound requires additional structure. We then show that a mild form of local invariance suffices. We prove that any such design that is invariant under unitary translations acting on a single qubit approximates Porter-Thomas to total variation distance $O(k^{-1/2}+\varepsilon)$. Every strong $\varepsilon$-approximate unitary $k$-design invariant on $\log k+O(1)$ qubits achieves error $2^{-Ω(k)}+O(\varepsilon)$ in Kolmogorov distance and $2^{-Ω(k)}+O(\varepsilon\log(2/\varepsilon))$ in total variation distance. These results identify the distributional accuracy guaranteed by moment matching and the structure that improves it. As an application, we show that the Shannon entropy of the output distribution of a strong $\varepsilon$-approximate $k$-design is concentrated around its Haar value $n-Θ(1)$: its mean differs from the Haar mean by $O(k^{-1/4}+\varepsilon^{1/2})$ and its standard deviation is $O(2^{-n/2}+k^{-1/8}+\varepsilon^{1/4})$. Consequently, a trusted device sampling such circuits generates $n-O(1)$ bits of entropy per sample, which makes them useful for random number generation.

papers.title: Robust and leakage-resilient device-independent oblivious transfer in MiniQCrypt
papers.abstract: Assuming post-quantum one-way functions, we construct device-independent oblivious transfer and bit commitment that tolerate independent honest faults at a constant rate and adaptive, bidirectional quantum leakage between the laboratories at a constant rate. Honest parties use trusted classical computation to operate untrusted quantum devices, which may share arbitrary entanglement and perform joint measurements without assumptions of independence or identical distribution. Security is simulation-based against quantum polynomial-time adversaries and composes sequentially with efficient simulators. For security parameter $λ$ and a prescribed total leakage budget $\ell$, one complete one-bit oblivious transfer uses $Θ(\ell+\log^2λ)$ device coordinates in at most three single-use device windows, including preprocessing, and polynomial classical computation and communication. The leakage budget is shared across these windows. The commitment has efficient simulators against both parties and yields device-independent coin tossing with abort; each uses one window. Completeness of oblivious transfer gives device-independent secure computation with abort for every efficiently computable classical functionality on a fixed number of parties, against static corruption of any proper subset, provided each reached call to oblivious transfer satisfies the device and budget conditions. The construction combines short selectors with code-based choice masking, a global audit, and error correction across field symbols. The commitment extractor changes a classical code coset while leaving the device execution and its leakage unchanged. Sender security uses a global Fourier analysis and a selector-aware Magic Square repetition bound derived from the two-round threshold theorem of Kundu and Tan (2023).

papers.title: Smooth perturbation theory and generic Cantor spectrum for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic operators
papers.abstract: We consider multi-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with monotone sawtooth-type potentials in the perturbative localization regime. We prove that a given gap is closed iff a corresponding (via a natural gap labeling) eigenfunction vanishes at the origin. Using this, we show that for a generic choice of the sampling function $f$, the spectrum of such an operator is a Cantor set, with all possible gaps being open. We also provide a class of functions $f$ for which some gaps are closed. Finally, we observe that certain gaps are more difficult to close than the others.

papers.title: Fast Quantum Algorithms for Learning Linear Threshold Functions
papers.abstract: Linear threshold functions (LTFs) are $\{-1,1\}$-valued functions $f_{w,θ}(x)=\text{sgn}(\langle w,x\rangle-θ)$, where $w\in\mathbb R^n$ has unit norm, $θ\in\mathbb R$, and $x\in\mathbb R^n$ or $\{-1,1\}^n$. If $θ=0$, the LTF is homogeneous, denoted $f_w=f_{w,0}$. LTFs are fundamental linear classifiers. We give three results: one for general LTFs and two for homogeneous LTFs. (1) With real-domain membership queries evaluating $f_{w,θ}(x)$ at any chosen $x\in\mathbb R^n$, we learn an LTF with classification error at most $\varepsilon$ under the standard Gaussian distribution using $O(\log(n/\varepsilon))$ queries and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ other gates. Classically, $Ω(n\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries are required, giving an exponential quantum query speedup. (2) A homogeneous LTF $f_w$ over $\{-1,1\}^n$ whose $k$ nonzero weights are equal and positive is Majority on the support of $w$. We identify this hidden support exactly using $O(\log k)$ queries, exponentially improving Belovs' $O(k^{1/4})$ upper bound. Our algorithm uses $O(n\log n\log k)$ gates and has $O(\log n\log k)$ non-oracle depth. Classical algorithms require $Ω(k\log(n/k))$ queries. (3) Suppose a unitary $U$ prepares discretized Gaussian quantum examples, corresponding to $\int_x\sqrt{γ_n(x)}|x\rangle|f_w(x)\rangle\,dx$. This is weaker than membership queries. Using the efficient quantum Hermite transform circuit, we learn homogeneous LTFs with classification error at most $\varepsilon$ under the Gaussian distribution using $O(n^{1/4}/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ applications of $U$ and $U^\dagger$ and $\widetilde{O}\!(\frac{n^{5/4}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}+\frac{n}{\varepsilon^2})$ other gates. Classically, $Ω(n/\varepsilon)$ examples are needed, giving a quartic quantum speedup in $n$. We show that the quantum query complexities in all three cases are optimal by proving matching lower bounds.

papers.title: Computational Bounds for $f$-Routing
papers.abstract: The $f$-routing protocol is a leading candidate for quantum position verification (Kent, Munro, and Spiller, Physical Review A, 2011), but security guarantees for explicit functions remain limited. We prove unconditional resource lower bounds for uniform attackers. Our techniques bypass communication-complexity bounds central to previous works, which are inherently at most linear in the input length. We show that, for input length $n$ and a sufficiently small constant $ε>0$, a uniform strategy running in time $T$ and succeeding with probability at least $1-ε$ on every input implies the following computational bounds on $f$. 1. If the strategies are arbitrary quantum channels, then $f\in \mathrm{QSZK}(\mathrm{poly}(T))$, where $\mathrm{QSZK}(T)$ is the class of languages having quantum statistical zero-knowledge proofs in which the verifier runs in time $T$ and the simulator in time $\mathrm{poly}(T)$. 2. If the strategies are Clifford+T circuits using at most $t$ magic gates, then $f\in \mathrm{DTIME}(\mathrm{poly}(T2^t))$. 3. If the strategies are explicit Pauli-sparse unitaries acting on at most $T$ qubits and having at most $s$ nonzero Pauli coefficients, then $f\in \mathrm{DTIME}(\mathrm{poly}(Ts))$. Time and space hierarchies then yield explicit functions secure against superlinear and even all polynomial-time adversaries under our computational restrictions. These bounds exceed the bounded-storage qubit bound $q\leq\log n$ of Bluhm, Christandl, and Speelman (Nature Physics, 2022) for the inner product function $f=\mathrm{IP}$, at the cost of restricting adversarial computation and increasing honest evaluation complexity.

papers.title: Single-shot state preparation thresholds in quantum LDPC codes: soundness, confinement, and statistical mechanics
papers.abstract: Single-shot error correction does not by itself establish equally direct and robust logical-state initialization. We study preparation of CSS quantum low-density parity-check code states using one noisy round of the code's checks. We prove that linear confinement over a weight range growing at least logarithmically, together with at least logarithmic distance, suffices for a nonzero threshold under independent local-stochastic readout and data noise in the relevant CSS sector. The threshold is certified by ideal recovery of a decoder-defined logical channel. The key is a correction rule that preserves the logical class under local syndrome changes, allowing the proof to proceed without a local-stochastic bound on the preparation residual. This gives a single-block guarantee for quantum expander codes without dimension jumps or batching. Under the stronger linear-soundness hypothesis, we establish local-stochastic residual noise, enabling composition with compatible fault-tolerant gadgets. For a retained-record formulation, we also derive an exact statistical-mechanical representation of optimal final recovery at fixed preparation decoder. A decoder-dependent logical-sector order parameter characterizes asymptotically successful block decoding. Monte Carlo results for the three-dimensional toric code provide finite-size evidence for a threshold beyond both linear sufficient conditions. These results distinguish logical robustness from local-stochastic residual-noise control and identify decoder consistency as a route to single-shot initialization.

papers.title: Anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping of thickness-quantized magnons
papers.abstract: Magnon damping is a key factor governing spin-wave transport and nonlinear dynamics of multimode magnon systems. However, many descriptions rely on the assumption of an effective mode-independent parameter, which can mask wavelength-dependent relaxation processes that depend on propagation geometry and mode profile. Here, we employ high-resolution parametric-instability spectroscopy to probe thickness-quantized spin waves with wavelengths down to about a hundred nanometers in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet films. The instability threshold exhibits a regular sawtooth dependence on the magnetic field, arising from switching between discrete thickness modes. Comparison with dipole--exchange theory reveals anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping that increases with mode number and depends differently on the in-plane and out-of-plane wavevector components.

papers.title: A Quantum Scaling Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Perfect Matching in General Graphs
papers.abstract: Quantum speed-ups have been obtained for many fundamental graph problems, including most variants of matching. A notable exception, however, is the maximum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) problem in general graphs with integer edge weights, which is arguably the most challenging variant of matching. We present a quantum algorithm for MWPM in general graphs that runs in $\widetilde{O}(n m^{2/3}\log W)$ time, where $W$ is an upper bound on the magnitude of the edge weights. This is an improvement over the best known classical combinatorial bound of $\widetilde{O}(m\sqrt n \log W)$ in the dense regime, where $m\ge n^{3/2}$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first quantum algorithm to obtain an asymptotic improvement over the best classical combinatorial algorithm for the MWPM problem in general graphs. The running time of our method accounts for QRAM initialization and access overheads up to polylogarithmic factors, as well as all classical updates to the data structures. At a high level, our algorithm is based on a classical framework due to Duan, Pettie, and Su, but our algorithm requires replacing certain classical tasks with quantum methods, alternative analysis of classical procedures, and the use of alternative data structures that can be implemented effectively in the QRAM model.

papers.title: Dynamic Coded Distributed Computing with Joint File Placement and Reduce Function Reassignment
papers.abstract: Coded distributed computing (CDC) mitigates the Shuffle communication bottleneck through coded multicast, but existing schemes with predetermined worker populations do not directly adapt to worker arrivals and disconnections. To address these dynamics, we propose a dynamic CDC scheme that preserves surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while exploiting the storage brought by arriving clusters. The model accommodates general MapReduce tasks under a placement that is partly fixed and partly new. The scheme uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays (PDAs) for file placement. A delivery-aware greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions, and a Communication Array allows workers with no Reduce function to serve as coded transmitters. For arbitrary feasible disconnections, the scheme's exact communication load is derived. A converse bound under one-shot communication shows that, in the absence of disconnections, the scheme lies within a factor of 2 of the lower bound under these assumptions when new clusters arrive, and within a factor of 4 otherwise.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(π_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Detuning-Controlled Proximity-Induced Localization and Reentrant Delocalization in a Quasiperiodic Ladder
papers.abstract: Proximity effects, in which one subsystem imprints its properties onto another, offer a route to controlling quantum matter. For localization, this raises the question of whether an extended system can be localized by its neighbor, and then delocalized again, in the regime of weak quasiperiodic disorder. Here, we demonstrate this behavior in a coupled Aubry--André ladder, where a staggered detuning applied to only one leg localizes the neighboring, undetuned leg through inter-leg hybridization, even before the detuned leg itself localizes. Upon further increasing the detuning, the undetuned leg undergoes re-entrant delocalization, while the detuned leg remains localized. Finite-size scaling supports the persistence of these regimes in the thermodynamic limit. On an IBM Quantum processor, we experimentally observe their dynamical signatures: strongly suppressed wave-packet spreading in the proximity-localized regime and its recovery upon re-entrant delocalization. Our results establish leg-selective detuning as a reversible control knob for localization and transport in coupled quantum systems.

papers.title: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States
papers.abstract: Solomonoff's universal inductive inference [Inf. Control. 1964] is one of the most general frameworks for learning from sequential data and predicting future observations. It provides prediction guarantees for any computable stochastic source. We ask whether an analogous universal theory of induction can be developed for quantum systems. To this end, we introduce universal quantum inductive inference, a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources that may exhibit arbitrary correlations and entanglement across time. Given the outcomes of past measurements and the corresponding post-measurement quantum systems, the learner produces a joint state that predicts the next measurement outcome and post-measurement system while preserving correlations with the past systems. We model a quantum source as a multipartite quantum state whose description is generated by an unknown $s$-bit program within a given time bound. The learner is required to produce a state that is $ε$-close in trace distance to the target with probability at least $1-δ$. We establish an information-theoretic inference algorithm with round complexity $O(sε^{-2}δ^{-1})$. We further prove a matching lower bound in the relevant parameter regime, even for classical sources. As a second result, we construct a non-i.i.d. state tomography algorithm that outputs a classical description of the conditional state of the next system given past measurement outcomes. Our information-theoretic tomography algorithm achieves round complexity $O(sn^2ε^{-4}δ^{-2})$, where $n$ is the number of qubits received in each round. Finally, we investigate the computational hardness of universal quantum inductive inference under quantum cryptographic assumptions.

papers.title: Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations and the analytic structure of strings in AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: The pole structure of string correlators in AdS$_3$ encodes essential information about the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. The corresponding residues for spectrally flowed three-point functions have been extracted from their exact expressions and shown to match the predictions of the holographic CFT. Away from the tensionless point, the latter is defined perturbatively in terms of a deformed symmetric orbifold. For $n$-point functions, such a matching has so far only been achieved for a specific subset of poles, and only by means of free-field techniques. Here we develop an alternative approach. We show that, starting from the localization properties of worldsheet correlators, one can solve the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations on the corresponding locus and perform the integration over worldsheet moduli explicitly for any $n$ and for arbitrary values of the spectral flow charges. In this way we reproduce, directly from the exact worldsheet theory and including the normalization, the residues previously obtained with free-field methods. We expect this to provide a systematic framework for computing the remaining residues and, ultimately, for determining the full analytic structure of string amplitudes in AdS$_3$.

papers.title: Short-Length Code Designs for Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Deep Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables joint communication and sensing using a shared waveform, but its signal design is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between the two objectives, particularly in the short blocklength regime. This paper proposes an autoencoder (AE)-based framework for ISAC waveform design in noncoherent settings. We derive a modified Cramér-Rao bound for multi-target delay estimation and analyze the maximum-likelihood decoding rule for noncoherent communication under correlated fading. These results reveal structural connections and trade-offs between communication and sensing objectives in waveform design. Based on this analysis, the AE learns waveform representations that jointly optimize both functionalities, with a tunable parameter controlling the trade-off. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms conventional schemes in both communication reliability and sensing accuracy, especially under short blocklength and fading conditions.

papers.title: Polar-metric/axial-gauge perturbations of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov wormhole
papers.abstract: We study linear perturbations of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov traversable wormhole in the sector where polar metric perturbations couple to axial gauge perturbations, and reduce it to two coupled master equations of Zerilli-Moncrief type. In the throat the Casimir energy of the lowest Landau level of charged fermions holds the wormhole open, and the linearised Bianchi identities hold only if the fermions respond. Once their state is fixed, their two-dimensional response follows from the conformal anomaly. We lift it to four dimensions on the field lines, assuming that the metric of each line scales with the local field strength. Through the trace anomaly this scaling couples the field strength to the worldsheet curvature, reminiscent of a Wen-Zee term. The response comes with a Hall current that sources the axial gauge mode. At zeroth order in the fermion backreaction $α$ the throat is AdS$_2\times S^2$ and the modes are two Poschl-Teller problems with squared masses $l(l-1)$ and $(l+1)(l+2)$. We give the $O(α)$ corrections in closed form. In the mouths the fermions act through the anomaly at the same order, and mouths and throat match. The higher Landau levels act through the one-loop Euler-Heisenberg action. We keep it to first order in $η_{\rm H}=g_c^2/12π^2$, which is not suppressed by $1/q$. It enlarges the AdS$_2$ radius and splits the levels shared by the two modes. On the closed-throat levels examined their $O(α)$ mixing is of second order. The $O(α)$ frequency shifts there, measured by the static observer at the throat centre, are real and depend on the assumed scaling, compared here with a lift on the coordinate planes. Region by region, at first order in $α$ and $η_{\rm H}$ and on the levels examined, we find no growing mode at $l=2,3,4$, although the $O(α)$ mouth rests on an estimate. Stability of the wormhole as a whole is not shown.

papers.title: Algebraic-Geometric Parvaresh--Vardy Subspace Designs and Rank Condensers
papers.abstract: A subspace design is a collection of subspaces $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ of $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ with the property that no low-dimensional subspace $W$ intersects the collection "too much". Subspace designs and related objects in linear-algebraic pseudorandomness have found a broad range of applications, ranging from list decoding to derandomizing algorithms. We construct explicit strong subspace designs over every finite field. In the extremal case where the co-dimension $t$ of each $H_i$ is equal to the dimension of $W$, for every constant field size our construction attains $n=Ω(k)$ and matches the probabilistic intersection bound up to a constant factor. All previous constructions required the field size to grow with $t$ (or $k$). Our subspace designs also imply new constructions of rank condensers over arbitrary finite fields. This result is the first to achieve an optimal dependence on $k$ while maintaining both a constant output entropy rate and a constant field size. As an application, we construct lossless rank extractors for linear sources of rank $r$, for all $r < q$, with parameters matching those of Guo, Raj, Shangguan and Zhang (FOCS '26), thereby generalizing their result to prime fields and smaller field sizes. Our construction is based on an algebraic-geometric version of the Parvaresh--Vardy codes (Parvaresh--Vardy FOCS '05, Guruswami ECCC '05), extending the framework underlying the condensers of Guruswami, Umans and Vadhan (JACM '09). We view our construction as a linear-algebraic analysis -- tailored to affine sources -- of the GUV construction, generalized to functions over algebraic curves. More specifically, inspired by Ta-Shma and Umans (CCC '12) we develop a two-level evaluation scheme, where we first evaluate a function on a curve at extension-field points, and then evaluate a corresponding affine-linear polynomial to obtain outputs over the base field.

papers.title: Learning Scattering Amplitudes with Transformer Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a transformer reinforcement learning algorithm that learns to solve high loop-level scattering amplitudes in planar N = 4 Super Yang-Mills theory. Our algorithm improves on previous transformer-only results by incorporating previously derived symmetries and relationships into the learning algorithm. This results in a greatly decreased fraction of the solution that needs to be known a priori to solve the entire problem. An additional benefit is that our algorithm also ensures that every output obeys the set of known relationships. Rather than predicting all coefficients independently, the model proposes assignments that are propagated through exact linear relations, while MCTS searches over assignments when propagation alone is insufficient. This is crucial to the generalization of machine learning approaches to higher loops, as without this, there is no way to overcome the factorially scaling of state sizes and compare to results derived via other methods. Using the symbology representation of the form factor, we frame the problem as learning a mapping between discrete sequences and integer coefficients.

papers.title: Topological Geometry of Neutrino Mass and Mixing
papers.abstract: This work presents an analytical, parameter-free derivation of the lepton mixing matrix and active neutrino mass spectrum from an icosahedral $A_5$ flavor manifold coupled to the three-generation Iwahori-Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$. Partitioning the icosahedral vertex curvature across the six fundamental Weyl chambers of $H_3(q)$ fixes an elementary angular defect $Δ_{AD} = π/18$, unifying ultra-high-energy mass generation and low-energy flavor mixing as dual realizations of a single geometric invariant. At the topological braiding threshold $μ\sim M_0$, the right-handed Majorana scale $M_0$ breaks scale invariance and drives the five-dimensional Temperley-Lieb quotient into its hyperbolic regime with loop modulus $d'_{AD} = 2\coshΔ_{AD}$, where Quantum Yang-Baxter Baxterization projects the algebraic roots onto a hierarchical heavy spectrum $M_1 > M_2 > M_3 > 0$. Integrating out and inverting these states via a flavor-isotropic Seesaw mechanism Type-I locks in the normal mass hierarchy with $m_1 \approx 3.64$ meV, $\sum_i m_i \approx 63.5$ meV, and $m_β\approx 9.45$ meV. Simultaneously, probability conservation requires analytic continuation onto the compact unitary circle, factorizing the mixing matrix into the $A_5$ Golden Ratio baseline, a unitary boundary twist generated by the longest Coxeter involution, and a discrete Majorana parity matrix. This geometry yields $θ_{13} = 8.49^\circ$, $θ_{12} = 32.11^\circ$, $θ_{23} = 45^\circ$, and maximal Dirac CP violation, $δ_{CP} = \pm π/2$, while discrete $SO(3)$ parities quantize the relative Majorana phases, $α_{13} = -π, α_{23} = 0$, preventing $0νββ$ decay cancellation, $m_{ββ} \approx 1.14$ meV, and suppressing renormalization group drift to $\dotθ_{ij} \sim 10^{-7}$ rad.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization with Fisher Information Geometry: Gradient Bounds and Trust-Region Methods
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian optimization (BO) through the lens of information geometry. Pulling back the Fisher information metric through the surrogate posterior map yields a local sensitivity tensor on the input space, which leads to an upper bound on the gradient of reparameterizable acquisition functions (AFs). This view explains vanishing-gradient behavior in high-dimensional BO and provides a common interpretation of heuristics such as RAASP and dimension-scaled lengthscales. The upper bound can also serve as a generic recipe to understand the behavior of new acquisition functions or surrogates in high input dimensions as well. Using the bounds, we also identify necessary conditions for an input location to be an optimizer of the AF for a univariate Gaussian predictive posterior. Building on this analysis, we propose FITR, a trust-region-based BO method that replaces lengthscale-based scaling with local pullback-Fisher weights. FITR is not restricted to GP kernels with explicit lengthscales and easily generalizes to non-isotropic surrogates. FITR shows competitive performance on several benchmarks.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage for Distributed Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: We present a distributed quantum algorithm that $3$-colors cycles in $O(1)$ rounds, with high probability. It follows that all locally checkable labeling problems (LCLs) that have round complexity $O(\log^* n)$ in the classical LOCAL model can be solved in $O(1)$ rounds in the quantum-LOCAL model, with high probability; this includes problems such as maximal independent set and maximal matching in bounded-degree graphs. This presents the first natural examples of graph problems with an asymptotic distributed quantum advantage for the LOCAL model; all prior examples that separate LOCAL and quantum-LOCAL are artificial problems constructed merely for the sake of demonstrating quantum advantage.

papers.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Testing Fourier Dimensionality
papers.abstract: A boolean function $f$ has Fourier dimension $k$ if its strings with nonzero Fourier coefficients span a subspace of dimension $k$. We first consider the property testing task of determining whether a function has Fourier dimension at most $k$, or is $ε$-far from being so. We show that there is an $O(k/\sqrtε)$-query quantum property tester for this problem, which we show to be almost optimal. Combined with Gopalan \etal's classical lower bound of $Ω(2^{k/2})$, this demonstrates an exponential quantum advantage for this task. We complement this result with a $\tilde{O}(2^{k/2}/ε)$ classical tester, giving a quadratic improvement over the previous best tester, and essentially settling the classical query complexity. We then introduce and study the tolerant version of this problem. That is, determining whether a function is $αε$-close to having Fourier dimension at most $k$, or is $ε$-far from being so. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that this tolerant version of the problem is essentially just as hard as the standard version of the problem. That is, we show this problem has a $\tilde{O}(k/ε)$ quantum tester, and a $\tilde{O}(2^{k/2}/ε)$ classical tester.

papers.title: Quantum Generative Modeling with a Coherent Memory, Exact Training and a Memory-Dimension Advantage
papers.abstract: We introduce the coherent memory Born machine (CoMB), an algorithm for quantum generative modeling on a register whose size does not depend on the dimension of the data. CoMB generates a sample one component per round. In each round, a work register is entangled with a memory register and measured, and the outcome gives one component. The memory is never measured and carries correlations between rounds. We show that the characteristic function of the generated distribution is a product of small matrices, one per round. This gives exact training, with maximum mean discrepancy losses and gradients costing time linear in the data dimension, without sampling or likelihood. We also compile every round onto one work qubit and evaluate device noise exactly. To isolate coherence, each CoMB is compared with its dephased twin and with equally trained classical hidden Markov models. We benchmark it on continuous data, $368$-cell calorimeter showers from five qubits, and on sequential data, handwritten digits from three qubits. The coherent memory provides a memory-dimension advantage. Four coherent levels do the work of about six classical states on both benchmarks, and of at least five with $95\%$ confidence on showers at every training budget, including convergence. On showers, removing their coherence raises the loss by $23$ to $31\%$. With eight levels, where all models approach a common floor, coherent and classical memories become indistinguishable with longer training. On an IBM Heron processor, the memory carries two thirds of the inter-round correlation through twelve mid-circuit measurements.

papers.title: Exponentially Larger Deletion-Correcting Codes and Constant-List-Decodable Insertion-Deletion Codes
papers.abstract: We establish improved asymptotic rate bounds for adversarial insertion--deletion codes. For binary unique-deletion correction in the linear-deletion regime, we strictly improve Levenshtein's classical lower-bound expression. At deletion fraction $δ=0.1$, our achievable rate increases from $0.162009$ to $0.194890$, a relative gain of approximately $20.30\%$. For list decoding with any prescribed finite list size $L$, we obtain new achievable-rate bounds for binary deletion and insertion codes. Our approach combines the Lovász local lemma with refined counting of common subsequences and supersequences, using generating functions and run-restricted sampling. We also establish a combinatorial reduction that trades $L$ units of insertion budget for one unit of deletion budget without changing the code or increasing the list size. It transfers insertion lower bounds at $γ+Lδ$ and deletion upper bounds at $δ+γ/L$ to mixed errors. We also derive a run-counting Levenshtein-type list-decoding upper bound and a higher-order Elias-type upper bound. The latter recovers Yasunaga's asymptotic unique-decoding bound at $L=1$ and strictly improves the Haeupler--Shahrasbi--Sudan insertion upper bound for every fixed $L$ and $0<γ<q-1$. Numerical comparisons quantify the gains and the remaining gaps.

papers.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
papers.abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $λ_L$. Thus $λ_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.

papers.title: A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
papers.abstract: Faster quantum gates can reduce the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors, speeding up gates often involves stronger microwave pulses, which can increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that gate transition rates at fixed trace distance between the initial and final system states grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under pulse-uniformity conditions, without assuming an upper bound on the coupling strength. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.

papers.title: Deterministic Hypergraph SYK: Melonic Dominance and Maximal Chaos Without Disorder Averaging
papers.abstract: We show that the leading melonic structure of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model can be realized by a single sparse Majorana Hamiltonian, without disorder averaging. In our deterministic hypergraph SYK model (hSYK), $N$ Majorana fermions interact through $O(dN)$ terms with uniform couplings, arranged on a fixed $q$-uniform, $d$-regular hypergraph. If the hypergraph is linear, has few short cycles, and is a spectral expander, then at large $d$ the two-point function obeys the melonic Schwinger-Dyson equation site by site. The leading thermodynamics are therefore those of SYK, and at leading order in $1/d$ every bilocal fluctuation other than the Schwarzian is gapped. The four-point ladder splits into scrambling modes labeled by eigenvalues of the site adjacency operator. At strong coupling, the uniform mode is maximally chaotic, and a non-uniform mode grows only if its eigenvalue exceeds $1/(q-1)$. Exact diagonalization of single instances with $N\le24$ agrees with the melonic two-point function and thermodynamics more closely than dense SYK of the same size, shows Wigner-Dyson level statistics, and reproduces the predicted mode structure of out-of-time-order correlators. Numerically, random linear hypergraphs typically satisfy these conditions, and for $d>q$ also avoid emergent symmetries. The model is a natural candidate for quantum simulation.

papers.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: A Local Type IIB D3--D7--D3 Mechanism for Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
papers.abstract: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate a local Type IIB D3$_+$--D7--D3$_-$/E3 mechanism for generating perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Under explicitly stated microscopic conditions, the E3 instanton generates fermion mixing with both scalar and pseudoscalar components. The pseudoscalar component reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. The analysis also provides a model-building roadmap toward a compact phenomenological realization. Such a realization requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode capable of mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.

papers.title: Predictive Structure Behind Rare Outcomes in Random Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Local random quantum circuits can occasionally produce unusually large output probabilities. However, the final output distribution containing such a peak does not by itself reveal how the peak formed during circuit evolution. We investigate whether states formed during circuit evolution carry structural signatures that predict subsequent peak formation. In numerical experiments, circuits selected for large terminal peaks exhibit stronger pairwise correlations and probability redistribution, together with lower bipartite entanglement and output entropy, than controls generated by the same random-circuit model. Their intermediate states retain higher fresh-peak event probability when the remaining gates are independently regenerated. Within an unconditioned ensemble, a fixed structural score computed from the initial circuit segment predicts new-peak probability. Averaged equally across n=8-16, a replay with equal numbers of remaining-circuit evaluations shows that score-based allocation yields 1.80 times as many peaks as uniform allocation and about 18% more than a fixed baseline based on probability concentration and redistribution. Randomizing relative phases while preserving computational-basis probabilities strongly attenuates the selected-state advantage, demonstrating a functional contribution from relative-phase organization. Controlled gate-selection tests further show that the identified structure can guide circuit construction to promote peak formation. Together, these results connect rare output events to intermediate-state structure with predictive and constructive value under finite-depth local dynamics.

papers.title: Finite-Sample FDR Control for Greedy Aggregation over Networks
papers.abstract: Distributed multiple testing asks $N$ sites, each holding p-values for its own hypotheses, to control the false discovery rate (FDR) of the discoveries made across the whole network while communicating only a small number of bits. Greedy interval aggregation (Pournaderi and Xiang, IEEE TSIPN, 2023) meets the communication budget but controls FDR only asymptotically, and its FDR can exceed the target at finite sample sizes; the same interval counts both select the rejection regions and calibrate the stopping rule, which biases the selected interval densities upward. We propose \emph{budgeted BONuS-GA}: each site mixes synthetic uniform p-values into its data, the center ranks candidate p-value intervals across sites using the pooled counts, and each site's false discoveries are estimated from its own synthetic counts under a per-site share of the level. The procedure needs no knowledge of the null proportions, uses every p-value for both selection and inference, and controls $FDR\leα$ at every sample size for any fixed assignment of hypotheses to sites, assuming only that the null p-values are independent uniforms, independent of the non-null p-values. It keeps the original $O(\sqrt m\log m)$ communication, $m$ being the total number of p-values, when $N=O(\sqrt m)$. We also give a sample-splitting alternative, cross-fit greedy aggregation, with finite-sample control under a random-site model, and we quantify the selection bias behind the original procedure's failure. In a monitoring-network simulation the budgeted procedure retains most of the power of its heuristic counterpart at moderate-to-large site sizes.
