papers.title: Direct signatures of Anderson orthogonality catastrophe in nonequilibrium quantum dots
papers.abstract: We propose schemes for unambiguous direct observation of Anderson orthogonality catastrophe (AOC) effects in a quantum dot coupled to a charge detector, enabling experimental estimation of the AOC exponent $α$. We show that certain easy-to-measure observables have a robust dependence on $α$ in the non-equilibrium regimes of source-drain voltage bias or thermal imbalance. Our results are obtained using a rate equation formalism in which the AOC effects on tunnel rates are incorporated in an exact manner, and directly support recent experimental results.

papers.title: Competing Bandits in Matching Markets via Super Stability
papers.abstract: We study bandit learning in matching markets with two-sided reward uncertainty, extending prior research primarily focused on single-sided uncertainty. Building on Irving's (1994) concept of super-stability and the partial-order proposal algorithm of Cseh and Juhos (2021), we use a simultaneous Extended Gale-Shapley procedure to certify stable matchings from incomplete preference information. By employing this procedure, our centralized algorithm attains logarithmic pessimal stable regret dependent on an instance-dependent admissible gap parameter. This algorithm is further adapted to a decentralized setting with a time-independent additive $O(N^3K)$ regret increase under the stated shared-flag communication model. Finally, we establish a centralized instance-dependent lower bound for binary stable regret on strict interior Bernoulli instances, elucidating the roles of admissible partial ranks and super-stable matching in characterizing the complexity of stable matching with bandit feedback.

papers.title: The Primakoff effect: The Axion-Photon Mixing in the Context of Stellar Plasma Physics
papers.abstract: We propose in this work the study of the production of axions in stellar plasma medium through an external magnetic field. In the background field approximation, we can show that the presence of the external magnetic field induces a mixing between the photon and the axion, i.e. the so called Primakoff effect. Since the axion is one of the greatest candidates for dark matter, for being a neutral pseudo-scalar field, the Primakoff process constitutes a mechanism (or portal) to access the dark sector, which in turn provides us new perspectives beyond the standard model. In the high energies limit, observables like probabilities transitions and particles production rates were computed.

papers.title: Perturbative Kähler Moduli Inflation
papers.abstract: In this work, we present two classes of inflationary models in the framework of type IIB string theory. The inflatons correspond to blow-up Kähler modulus arising from compactifying type IIB string theory on a Calabi-Yau. Using perturbative corrections, we first highlight a procedure for stabilising more than one Kähler modulus. For the case of two Kähler moduli, we explicitly construct two classes of inflationary potentials within the Kähler cone which satisfy both EFT and cosmological constraints. The first class of models, arising from moduli redefinition of the blow-up mode, garners a potential of the form $V(φ)=V_{0}(1+C_{1} φ^{2/3})$ align with CMB data with tensor-to-scalar ratio $r\lesssim 10^{-2}$. The second class of models, which have been recently proposed as loop blow-up inflation, have a form $V(φ)=V_{0}(1+C_{2}φ^{-2/3})$, also agrees with CMB data with tensor-to-scalar ratio $r\lesssim 10^{-8}$. Our work differs from the original loop blow-up inflation in terms of stabilization mechanism and subsequently the tensor-to-scalar ratio.

papers.title: New exact solutions of the 3D Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: Previously we found a unique quantum system with a positive gauge-invariant Weyl-Stratonovich quasi-probability density function which can be defined by the so-called «quadratic funnel» potential. In this work we have constructed a class of exact solutions to the 3D Schrödinger equation for a two-parameter «quadratic funnel» potential based on the $Ψ$ -model of micro and macro systems. It should be noted that the Aharonov-Bohm effect is inherent in the quantum $Ψ$ -model. Explicit expressions for the energy spectrum and the set of eigenfunctions have been found. Using gauge invariance for scalar and vector potentials, a solution to the electromagnetic Schrödinger equation has been obtained, with a magnetic field in the form of a «Dirac string» defined by a singular vortex probability flux field. Superpositions of eigenfunctions leading to various types of vortex and potential probability current fields have been investigated in detail. The analysis of the quantum system's properties has been carried out within the Wigner-Vlasov formalism.

papers.title: Improving the Dynamic Range of Interacting Quantum Sensors via Optimized Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Interacting spin ensembles are promising platforms for quantum sensing, but spin-spin interactions can induce complex, nonmonotonic responses to external fields, limiting the dynamic range over which the fields can be estimated unambiguously. Here, we propose a quantum-circuit-learning-inspired method to improve the dynamic range of interacting quantum sensors using optimized global control fields. We consider an ensemble of dipole-coupled spins subjected to an inhomogeneous magnetic field generated by an electric current. By optimizing the global control fields applied during sensing, we train the expectation value of the collective magnetization to approximate a prescribed monotonic target function. We also introduce a penalty on the magnetization variance to account for measurement fluctuations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the optimized control can substantially enlarge the dynamic range compared with sensing without control. We further investigate the trade-off between dynamic range and estimation uncertainty and show that the variance penalty can reduce the uncertainty at the expense of dynamic range. These results demonstrate that learning-assisted global control provides a promising approach to improving the performance of interacting quantum sensors.

papers.title: Optical vortex generation by magnons with spin-orbit-coupled light
papers.abstract: Light possesses both spin and orbital angular momentum. In spatially asymmetric optical fields, these properties undergo spontaneous coupling, referred to as optical spin-orbit coupling. The study of the coupling has recently become central in modern optics due to its substantial applications in communications, sensing, and quantum control. A key challenge is to clarify the relationship between the origins of spatially asymmetric optical fields and the resulting spin-orbit coupling. Current research focuses on materials and configurations exhibiting spatial asymmetry, such as focusing lenses, interfaces, inhomogeneous media, and metasurfaces. However, Maxwell's equations indicate that matter can introduce both spatial and temporal asymmetry into optical fields. For instance, magnetic ordering breaks the time-reversal symmetry of interacting optical fields via the magneto-optic effect, introducing nonreciprocity in the resulting optical phenomena. Despite the importance, optical phenomena involving both spatially and temporally asymmetric optical fields remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that breaking time and spatial symmetries through magnons and light focusing, respectively, transforms an input Gaussian beam into a specific optical vortex beam in a nonreciprocal manner. This phenomenon is quantitatively explained by integrating the physics of magnon-induced Brillouin light scattering with optical spin-orbit coupling. The observed conservation of total angular momentum, encompassing both magnons and photons, further indicates that magnons can control both spin and orbital angular momentum of light. Finally, we outline future research directions enabled by asymmetric optical fields in both space and time.

papers.title: Analytic approaches to anisotropic holographic superfluids in asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry
papers.abstract: We explore anisotropic holographic superfluidity and find analytic solutions near critical point where superfluid/normalfluid phase transition appears in a holographic dual fluid system. In arXiv:hep-th/1109.4592, the authors obtained such an analytic solution in 5-dimensional Einstein-SU(2)Yang-Mills system, and it is asymptotically AdS$_5$. What is more in this note is that we get analytic solutions near the critical point in 3- and 4- dimensional Einstein-Scalar-U(1)$\times$SU(2)Yang-Mills systems, which become asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry. We also get leading order back reactions to the background geometry, which clearly shows spatial anisotropy of the bulk geometry. To explore the properties of the spacetime, we compute holographic entanglement entropy and confirm that the superfluid/normalfluid phase transition must occur at the critical point.

papers.title: Contact diagrams for chords
papers.abstract: We demonstrate how contact chord diagrams can arise from certain Fock-space models and compute the corresponding correlation functions using the chord path integral technique. In particular, our three-point functions are in the right form dictated by conformal symmetry, and some of our four-point functions match the results of some AdS$_2$ contact Witten diagrams.

papers.title: IterTestQ: Assembly-Level, Cross-Platform Testing of Quantum Computing Platforms
papers.abstract: Quantum computing platforms are susceptible to quantum-specific bugs, such as incorrectly ordering qubits or incorrectly implementing quantum abstractions. These bugs are difficult to detect and require specialized expertise. The field faces challenges due to a fragmented landscape of platforms and rapid development cycles that often prioritize new features over thorough testing, severely hindering the reliability of quantum software. To address these challenges, we present IterTestQ, a novel cross-platform testing approach for quantum computing platforms. The key technical contribution is our novel ITE process, which generates equivalent quantum programs by iteratively (I)mporting them into platform-specific representations, (T)ransforming the program via optimizations and gate conversions, and (E)xporting the program again. To transfer programs across platforms and test cross-platform consistency, IterTestQ leverages QASM, an assembly-level representation supported by most platforms. The approach uses a crash oracle to detect failures during cross-platform transformations and an equivalence oracle to validate the semantic consistency of the generated assembly programs, which are expected to be equivalent by construction. We evaluate IterTestQ on widely-used quantum computing platforms, including Qiskit, PennyLane, Pytket, BQSKit, and Cirq, revealing 23 bugs, 17 of which are already confirmed or fixed. Our results also demonstrate that IterTestQ complements existing quantum fuzzers (covering tens of thousands of otherwise uncovered lines), is efficient (with 0.00089 seconds per generated program), and that the ITE process is crucial for its effectiveness.

papers.title: Noise Mitigation in Single Microwave Photon Counting by Cascaded Quantum Measurements
papers.abstract: Single-photon detection in the microwave domain has recently emerged as a powerful tool for quantum sensing, offering a path beyond the standard quantum limit of linear amplification since their sensitivity is set by their dark-count rate rather than by the vacuum fluctuations of the detected field. Superconducting qubit-based single microwave photon detectors (SMPDs) encode the absorption of itinerant photons into discrete quantum states via engineered, non-destructive interactions. A previously demonstrated implementation based on four-wave mixing achieved high efficiency, but remained limited by residual qubit excitation and thermal noise at the detector input. Here, we propose and demonstrate a new SMPD that relies on two cascaded four-wave mixing processes. The information on photon detection is encoded on two spatially separated qubits, which mitigates noise due to uncorrelated qubit errors. Furthermore, increasing the detection frequency up to 11.7 GHz reduces input thermal noise. These combined advances lead to a record-low power sensitivity of $2.4 \cdot 10^{-23}\mathrm{W}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ over a bandwidth of $230\ \mathrm{kHz}$.

papers.title: Models of liquid-sample confinement for nanoscale NMR
papers.abstract: Diffusion is a prominent source of noise affecting nuclear magnetic resonance at the nanometer scale (nano-NMR), preventing high-resolution studies of unpolarized liquid samples and hindering the development of nanofluid devices. Actively managing diffusion noise through sample confinement is likely to unveil alternative noise sources that have so far been disregarded, as they occur in longer timescales and consequently are masked by diffusion. These secondary noise sources could diminish the advantages provided by sample confinement, but they may also yield valuable information about the behavior of the fluid sample and its interactions with the confinement device. In this article, we study in detail two previously unaccounted noise models for confined nano-NMR, namely, surface interactions and porosity, and discuss their implications for typical nano-NMR experiments.

papers.title: Certification of quantum correlations at arbitrary distances through routed Bell tests
papers.abstract: Transmission loss represents a major obstacle to the device-independent certification of quantum correlations over long distances, limiting applications such as device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD). In this work, we investigate the recently proposed concept of routed Bell experiments, in which a particle sent to one side can be measured either near or far from the source. We prove that routed Bell tests involving only entangled qubits can certify quantum correlations even in the presence of arbitrary loss on the channel to the distant device. This is achieved by adapting concepts from self-testing and quantum steering to the routed Bell test framework. Finally, as a natural extension of our approach, we outline a DIQKD protocol that, in principle, is secure over arbitrary distances.

papers.title: Demystifying 5G Polar and LDPC Codes: A Comprehensive Review and Foundations
papers.abstract: Understanding how 5G networks correct errors is no trivial matter. At the heart of the process lie two sophisticated families of codes: LDPC and polar codes. This paper opens the black box, not only by explaining how these codes are designed, but also by showing how they are encoded and decoded in practice. To describe the research covered in this review, we present a detailed survey of the literature supplemented with insights that are often buried deep within technical standards. These foundations are not just historical footnotes: they remain relevant to research on error correction for future wireless systems. In bringing clarity to these building blocks, we aim to help engineers and researchers navigate what is both a complex and increasingly vital part of wireless communication.

papers.title: Relatively-Secure LLM-Based Steganography via Constrained Markov Decision Processes for High-Efficiency Embedding
papers.abstract: Linguistic steganography aims to conceal information within natural language text without being detected. An effective steganography approach should encode the secret message bits into a minimal number of language tokens while preserving the natural appearance and fluency of the stego-texts. We present a new framework to enhance the embedding efficiency by framing the steganographic embedding procedure as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP), which takes into consideration the long-term dependencies instead of merely the immediate effects. We constrain the solution space such that the discounted expected cumulative total variation between the selected conditional probability distribution and the original one given by the LLM is below a threshold. To find the optimal policy, we first show that the functional optimization problem can be simplified to a convex problem with a finite number of variables. For the binary-state model, we give a full characterization of the optimal policy, including closed-form expressions in several regimes, and show that it displays water-filling-like behavior in certain cases. The solution indicates that states with highly deterministic transition distributions are preferable for adjustment in the binary-state case. For larger state spaces, the optimal solution is more complex and explicit solutions are difficult to obtain, but the optimal policies show similar structural behaviors.

papers.title: On the Optimality of Gaussian Code-books for Signaling over a Two-Users Weak Gaussian Interference Channel
papers.abstract: This article establishes that the capacity region of the two-users weak Gaussian interference channel can be achieved using Gaussian codebooks. It is further shown that the upper concave envelope of the achievable rate region can be attained using at most two time-sharing phases. In one phase, both users transmit simultaneously, while in the second phase, when present, only one user is active. Furthermore, the boundary of the capacity region can be traversed continuously through incremental reallocations of power between the two messages transmitted by each user. Finally, it is proven that the Han-Kobayashi achievable rate region with single-letter Gaussian codebooks attains the optimal boundary of the capacity region.

papers.title: Polarons in atomic gases and two-dimensional semiconductors
papers.abstract: In this work we provide a comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental studies of the properties of polarons formed by mobile impurities strongly interacting with quantum many-body systems. We present a unified perspective on the universal concepts and theoretical techniques used to characterize polarons in two distinct platforms, ultracold atomic gases and atomically-thin transition metal dichalcogenides, which are linked by many deep parallels. We review polarons in both fermionic and bosonic environments, highlighting their similarities and differences including the intricate interplay between few- and many-body physics. Various kinds of polarons with long-range interactions or in magnetic backgrounds are discussed, and the theoretical and experimental progress towards understanding interactions between polarons is described. We outline how polaron physics, regarded as the low density limit of quantum mixtures, provides fundamental insights regarding the phase diagram of complex condensed matter systems. Furthermore, we describe how polarons may serve as quantum sensors of many-body physics in complex environments. Our work highlights the open problems, identifies new research directions and provides a comprehensive framework for this rapidly evolving research field.

papers.title: Highest weight vectors, shifted topological recursion and quantum curves
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of topological recursion by considering Airy structures whose partition functions are highest weight vectors of particular $\mathcal{W}$-algebra representations. Such highest weight vectors arise as partition functions of Airy structures only under certain conditions on the representations. In the spectral curve formulation of topological recursion, we show that this generalization amounts to adding specific terms to the correlators $ ω_{g,1}$, which leads to a ``shifted topological recursion'' formula. We then prove that the wave-functions constructed from this shifted version of topological recursion are WKB solutions of families of quantizations of the spectral curve with $ \hbar$-dependent terms. In the reverse direction, starting from an $\hbar$-connection, we find that it is of topological type if the exact same conditions that we found for the Airy structures are satisfied. When this happens, the resulting shifted loop equations can be solved by the shifted topological recursion obtained earlier.

papers.title: Refining Concentration Bounds for Gaussian Quadratic Chaos with Applications
papers.abstract: This paper studies concentration of measure for Gaussian quadratic chaos in the non-asymptotic regime. We begin by tightening the classic Hanson-Wright inequality, where we increase its absolute constant $κ$ from 0.125 to at least 0.1457 in the symmetric case. We present a sharper version of Laurent-Massart inequality (LMI), which increases $κ$ from the largest available value of $1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.134$ to $\frac{9-\sqrt{17}}{32}\approx 0.152$ in the positive-semidefinite case. We develop a sequence of inequalities indexed by $m\ge1$ that involve Schatten norms of the underlying matrix. The case $m=1$ recovers HWI. The bounds undergo a phase transition in the sense that if the tail parameter is smaller than a critical threshold $τ_c$, then $m=1$ is the tightest, whereas if it is larger than $τ_c$, then $m=\infty$ is the tightest. This leads to a novel bound called the $m_\infty$ bound. All HWI, LMI and the $m_\infty$ inequality rely on Markov's inequality. By avoiding Markov's inequality, we introduce the strong and weak $χ^2$ inequalities. We provide a list of concentration bounds that depend only on the operator norm in the positive-definite case, namely, the $m_\infty$ bound, the weak $χ^2$ bound, relaxed versions of HWI and LMI, and the so-called large-deviations bound. The sharpest among these is shown to be always either the $m_\infty$ bound or the weak $χ^2$ bound. By utilizing conditioning, modified versions of $m_\infty$, $χ^2$, and HW inequalities of various orders are proposed, all of which can be significantly tighter than the original inequalities. By leveraging the Ruben-Kotz expansion for the distribution of a positive-definite quadratic form, we introduce the Ruben-Kotz inequalities (RKIs) for general symmetric quadratic forms. A key advantage of RKIs is that they provide an explicit upper bound on the approximation gap.

papers.title: The entanglement membrane in 2d CFT: reflected entropy, RG flow, and information velocity
papers.abstract: The time evolution of entanglement entropy in generic chaotic many-body systems has an effective description in terms of a minimal membrane, characterised by a tension function. For 2d CFTs, a degenerate tension function reproduces several results regarding the dynamics of the entropy; this stands in contrast to higher dimensions where the tension is non-degenerate. In this paper we use holography to show that, in order to correctly capture the reflected entropy in 2d CFT, one needs to add an additional degree of freedom to the membrane description. Furthermore, we show that the conventional non-degenerate membrane tension function emerges upon introducing a relevant deformation of the CFT, dual to a planar BTZ black hole with scalar hair and with an interior Kasner universe. Finally, we also study the membrane description for reflected entropy and information velocity arXiv:1908.06993 in higher dimensions.

papers.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
papers.abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.

papers.title: Comments on Celestial CFT and $AdS_{3}$ String Theory
papers.abstract: In a recent work, Ogawa et al. (2024) proposed a model for celestial conformal field theory (CFT) based on the $H_{3}^{+}$-Wess-Zumino-Novikov-Witten (WZNW) model. In this paper, we extend the model advanced by Ogawa et al. (2024), demonstrating how it can holographically generate tree-level MHV scattering amplitudes for both gluons and gravitons when analytically continued to the ultra-hyperbolic Klein space $\mathbf{R}_{2}^{2}$, thereby offering an alternative to celestial Liouville theory. We construct a holographic dictionary in which vertex operators and conformal primaries in celestial CFT are derived from their worldsheet counterparts in Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ (bosonic) string theory. Within this dictionary, we derive the celestial stress-energy tensor, compute the two- and three-point functions, and determine the celestial operator product expansion (OPE). Additionally, we derive a system of partial differential equations that characterises the celestial amplitudes of our model, utilising the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations and worldsheet Ward identities. In the Appendix, we provide a concise introduction to the $H_{3}^{+}$-WZNW model, with emphasis on its connection to Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ string theory.

papers.title: Memory-Augmented Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) is an effective method for predicting chaotic systems by using a high-dimensional dynamic reservoir with fixed internal weights, while keeping the learning phase linear, which simplifies training and reduces computational complexity compared to fully trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses the exponential growth of Hilbert spaces in quantum systems, allowing for greater information processing, memory capacity, and computational power. However, the original QRC proposal requires coherent injection of inputs multiple times, complicating practical implementation. We present a hybrid quantum-classical approach that implements memory through classical post-processing of quantum measurements. This approach avoids the need for multiple coherent input injections and is evaluated on benchmark tasks, including the chaotic Mackey-Glass time series prediction. We tested our model on two physical platforms: a fully connected Ising model and a Rydberg atom array. The optimized model demonstrates promising predictive capabilities, achieving a higher number of steps compared to previously reported approaches.

papers.title: Amortized Stabilizer Rényi Entropy of Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract: Magic states are essential resources for fault-tolerant quantum computation. We introduce the amortized stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), which quantifies the largest SRE increase generated by a unitary, including arbitrary pure inputs and reference systems. Initial nonstabilizerness can enhance this increase, whereas analogous amortized logarithmic robustness and extent collapse to stabilizer-input optimizations. We establish structural properties and exact amortized 2-SRE values for the $T$ and $CCZ$ gates. We then derive explicit lower bounds on approximate $T$-state cost, with diamond-distance error, allowing stabilizer ancillary states, Pauli measurements, and classical feedforward. A Choi-state witness gives computable bounds for quantum Fourier transforms, controlled rotations, fractional controlled-SWAP gates, and finite Heisenberg-chain evolutions. We distinguish the unrestricted optimization from its Choi witness and specify the access and precision requirements for estimating Pauli moments. An odd-moment variant yields a confidence-qualified cost witness from ordinary copies.

papers.title: 6d Large Charge and 2d Virasoro Blocks
papers.abstract: We compute observables in the interacting rank-one 6d $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT at large R-charge. We focus on correlators involving $Φ^n$, namely symmetric products of the bottom component of the supermultiplet containing the stress-tensor. By using the moduli space effective action and methods from the large-charge expansion, we compute the OPE coefficients $\langleΦ^nΦ^mΦ^{n+m}\rangle$ in an expansion in 1/n. The coefficients of the expansion are only partially determined from the 6d perspective, but we manage to fix them order-by-order in 1/n numerically by utilizing the 6d/2d correspondence. This is made possible by the fact that this $6d$ observable can be extracted in 2d from a specific double-scaling limit of the vacuum Virasoro block, which can be efficiently computed numerically. We also extend the computation to higher-rank SCFTs, and discuss various applications of our results to 6d as well as 2d.

papers.title: Building blocks for $W$-algebras of classical types
papers.abstract: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,3,4,\dots)$ serves as a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$ in the sense that under mild hypothesis, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $W_{\infty}$. There is an $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ family of such $1$-parameter vertex algebras which, after tensoring with a Heisenberg algebra, are known as $Y$-algebras. They were introduced by Gaiotto and Rapčák and are expected to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras in type $A$, i.e., every $W$-(super) algebra in type $A$ is an extension of a tensor product of finitely many $Y$-algebras. Similarly, the orthosymplectic $Y$-algebras are $1$-parameter quotients of a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,4,6,\dots)$, which is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,4,\dots, 2N)$ for some $N$. Unlike type $A$, these algebras are not all the building blocks for $W$-algebras of types $B$, $C$, and $D$. In this paper, we construct a new universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra of type $W(1^3, 2, 3^3, 4, 5^3,6,\dots)$ which we denote by $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ since it contains a copy of the affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak{sp}_2)$. We identify $8$ infinite families of $1$-parameter quotients of $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ which are analogues of the $Y$-algebras. We regard $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ as a fundamental object on equal footing with $W_{\infty}$ and $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$, and we give some heuristic reasons for why we expect the $1$-parameter quotients of these three objects to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras of classical types. Finally, we prove that $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ has many quotients which are strongly rational. This yields new examples of strongly rational $W$-superalgebras.

papers.title: Computational quantum transport: a scattering approach perspective
papers.abstract: This review is devoted to the different techniques that have been developed to compute the phase-coherent transport properties of quantum nanoelectronic systems connected to electrodes. Beside a review of the different algorithms proposed in the literature, we provide a comprehensive and pedagogical derivation of the two formalisms on which these techniques are based: the scattering approach and the (nonequilibrium) Green's function approach. We show that the scattering problem can be formulated as a system of linear equations and that different existing algorithms for solving this scattering problem amount to different sequences of Gaussian elimination. We explicitly prove the equivalence of the two formalisms. We discuss the stability and numerical complexity of the existing methods. The review ends with a selection of a few applications where numerical calculations were instrumental in shaping our understanding of the physics.

papers.title: Which Structures Carry Information? The Inverse Problem of Heredity and a Computational Test in Digital Evolution
papers.abstract: The laws of physics do not label molecules as genes or physical patterns as computer programs. Yet some configurations are copied and, through shared machinery, determine what other structures are built. Can we identify these information carriers without knowing beforehand what they are? We formulate their joint identification with hereditary organisation as the inverse problem of heredity. We introduce Causal Structure Sets (CSS), which represent persistent physical structures and their realised causal ancestry without preassigning hereditary roles. Our candidate criterion seeks coherent families exhibiting replication, variation, variant-dependent translation and continuing lineages. A conditional reconstruction of recipe transmission shows how the criterion can identify a family of transmitted knowledge under explicit physical assumptions. In an Avida-like digital-evolution simulator, we construct CSSs of 848,000-884,000 nodes per run from recorded dynamics and intervention replay. A restricted role-blind search finds candidate families of 4-6 instruction types in development runs. Applied unchanged to 40 previously unseen seeds, the method finds families in all 39 runs with births; 96.2% of 30,422 program swaps yield division times characteristic of the inserted program. The preregistered five-part test nevertheless fails on one endpoint in two runs: the reference definition excludes a heritable program without an assigned phenotype. These results establish computational feasibility and reproducibility of candidate detections in one simulated world, not the criterion's general specificity. CSS opens a route to discovering unfamiliar hereditary organisation, and ultimately to understanding how information-bearing systems emerge, persist and evolve.

papers.title: Effective eigenvalue approximation from moments for self-adjoint trace-class operators
papers.abstract: Spectral properties of bounded linear operators play a crucial role in several areas of mathematics and physics. For each self-adjoint, trace-class operator $O$ we define a set $Λ_n\subset \mathbb{R}$, and we show that it converges to the spectrum of $O$ in the Hausdorff metric under mild conditions. Our set $Λ_n$ only depends on the first $n$ moments of $O$. We show that it can be effectively calculated for physically relevant operators, and it approximates the spectrum well without diagonalization. We prove that using the above method we can converge to the minimal and maximal eigenvalues with super-exponential speed. We also construct monotone increasing lower bounds $q_n$ for the minimal eigenvalue (or decreasing upper bounds for the maximal eigenvalue). This sequence only depends on the moments of $O$ and a concrete upper estimate of its $1$-norm; we also demonstrate that $q_n$ can be effectively calculated for a large class of physically relevant operators. This rigorous lower bound $q_n$ tends to the minimal eigenvalue with super-exponential speed provided that $O$ is not positive semidefinite. As a by-product, we obtain computable upper bounds for the $1$-norm of $O$, too. Numerical examples demonstrate the relevance of our approximation in estimating entropy and negativity, which is useful, among others, in quantum optical and in open quantum system models. The results can be directly applicable to problems in quantum information, statistical mechanics, and quantum thermodynamics, where using traditional techniques based on diagonalization is impractical.

papers.title: Quantum Hall transformer in a quantum point contact over the full range of transmission
papers.abstract: A recent experiment [Cohen et al., Science 382, 542 (2023)] observed a robustly quantized $e^2/2h$ conductance in a quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall edges (a quantum Hall transformer), which then vanishes at low temperature. While this behavior can be described by a boundary sine gordon (BSG) model derived from electron tunneling, the microscopic motivation for such strong tunneling is unclear. We use an alternative model based on sliding charge density waves and a density inhomogeneity to clarify the BSG description and calculate the conductance over the full range of transmission. Using a perturbative method and a matrix product state calculation, we draw a quantitative connection between the BSG model and the physical quantum Hall system.

papers.title: Holographic RG Flows from Running Couplings
papers.abstract: We investigate the RG flow in the holographic setup and study new IR physics at the IR fixed point, when a relevant scalar operator deforms a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT). On the dual gravity side, the renormalization group (RG) flow from the UV to the IR CFT can be described by a scalar field rolling from an unstable to a stable equilibrium point. Specifically, to make the scale dependence of the RG flow more explicit, we study the running coupling constant obtained by solving the beta function. After considering a simple scalar potential, we study the change of the coupling constant and its effect on the ground state along the RG flow. We showed that the central charge monotonically decreases along the RG flow, and its value at the IR fixed point is determined by the conformal dimension of the deformation operator and the coupling constant at the IR fixed point. We further investigate how changing the ground state influences the two-point function and conformal dimension of a local operator in the probe limit.

papers.title: Resonant analogue configurations in atomic condensates
papers.abstract: As a contribution to a memorial volume, we provide a comprehensive discussion of resonant configurations in analogue gravity, focusing on its implementation in atomic condensates and combining review features with original insights and calculations. In particular, we jointly analyze the analogues of the Andreev and Hawking effects using a microscopic description based on the Bogoliubov approximation. We perform a detailed study of the thermality of the Andreev and Hawking spectra for canonical black-hole solutions, finding that both can be described by a gray-body distribution to a very good approximation. We contemplate several resonant scenarios whose efficiency to enhance anomalous scattering processes is compared to that of non-resonant setups. The presence of quantum signatures in analogue configurations, such as the violation of Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities or entanglement, is analyzed, observing that resonant configurations highly increase the entanglement signal, especially for the Andreev effect. We also discuss how these results have served as inspiration for the rapidly expanding field of quantum information in high-energy colliders. Finally, we study the physics of black-hole lasers as further examples of resonant analogue structures, distinguishing three stages in its time evolution. For short times, we compute the linear and non-linear spectrum for different models. For intermediate times, we generalize the current analysis of the BHL-BCL crossover. For long times, we discuss the emerging concept of spontaneous Floquet state and its potential implications.

papers.title: New horizons for inhomogeneous quenches and Floquet CFT
papers.abstract: A fruitful avenue in investigating out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is to abruptly change their Hamiltonian and study the subsequent evolution of their quantum state. If this is done once, the setup is called a quench, while if it is done periodically, it is called Floquet driving. We consider the solvable setup of a two-dimensional CFT driven by Hamiltonians built out of conformal symmetry generators: in this case, the quantum dynamics can be understood using two-dimensional geometry. We investigate how the dynamics is reflected in the holographic dual three-dimensional spacetime and find new horizons. We argue that bulk operators behind the new horizons are reconstructable by virtue of modular flow.

papers.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
papers.abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.

papers.title: Over-fitting Control in Deep Nonlinear Matrix Completion via Gradual Nonsmooth Regularization
papers.abstract: Conventional matrix completion methods exploit the underlying low-rank structure of a target matrix to recover its missing entries, but may be inadequate for capturing complex nonlinear dependencies. Deep neural networks have therefore been increasingly adopted for nonlinear matrix completion (NLMC). However, their high representational capacity, particularly in deep fully connected neural networks (FCNNs), can lead to over-fitting when training is restricted to incomplete observations. In this paper, we propose a Deep Neural Network with Nonsmooth Regularization (DNN-NSR) framework to address this issue by incorporating two complementary structural priors: sparsity of intermediate representations and low-rankness of layer-wise weight matrices. Specifically, the $\ell_1$-norm of hidden representations promotes sparse latent features, while the nuclear norm of weight matrices encourages low-rank layer-wise transformations. To optimize the resulting nonsmooth and nonconvex objective, we develop an extrapolated proximal gradient algorithm that employs soft-thresholding and singular-value thresholding to handle the two regularization terms, respectively. We further introduce a gradual regularization strategy that progressively increases the influence of these structural penalties during training. Under suitable assumptions, we establish convergence properties of the proposed algorithm toward a critical point of the training objective. The effectiveness of DNN-NSR is evaluated through extensive experiments on synthetic matrix recovery, single-image inpainting, and recommender systems using the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets. Comparisons with representative linear and nonlinear matrix completion methods demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to improve recovery performance by jointly exploiting sparse latent representations and low-rank network transformations.

papers.title: Linear optics and the problem of Bell-like state discrimination
papers.abstract: A linear optics-based scheme to implement various quantum information processing tasks is of paramount importance due to its ease of implementation and low noise. Many information-theoretic tasks depend on the successful discrimination of Bell states. A no-go theorem states that it is not possible to perfectly discriminate among the four Bell states when the measurement apparatus is restricted to linear optical elements. The success probability is only $50\%$. Using extra resources such as hyperentanglement, ancillary entanglement, and even a minimum amount of non-linearity, complete Bell-state discrimination can be achieved. The success probability for Bell-like state discrimination is only $25\%$. Bell-like states are non-maximally entangled two-qubit states that resemble Bell states in structure but have unequal Schmidt coefficients. We find that this can be boosted to $50\%$ using hyperentanglement, where extra ancillary degrees of freedom (DOF) of photons, such as polarization, momentum, or OAM, are also entangled along with the system DOF. This contrasts with Bell-state discrimination, where $100\%$ can be achieved. Furthermore, we find that using correlations in the photons' arrival times, all four Bell states can be distinguished with $100\%$ success probability, while for Bell-like state discrimination, it increases only to $37.5\%$ from $25\%$. We observe a similar contrast when using ancillary entangled photons. While the success probability for discriminating all four Bell states increases as $1-\frac{1}{2^N}$, where $N$ is the number of ancillary photon pairs, for Bell-like states, it depends on the state parameters and can be less than $25\%$ in some cases. Also, adding further ancillary photons decreases the success probability. We then show that using non-linear gadgets, namely SFG, $100\%$ success probability can be achieved even for Bell-like state discrimination.

papers.title: Enumerating Complexity Revisited
papers.abstract: We study the relation between deterministic and randomized $\textit{enumerating}$ Kolmogorov complexity of sets $S\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Let $D(S)$ be the length of a shortest input on which a fixed optimal deterministic machine enumerates $S$, and let $ R(S) $ be the probability that a fixed optimal randomized machine enumerates $S$. It is easy to see that $-\log R(S) \le D(S)+O(\log D(S))$ for every $S$; the converse direction is much harder. Solovay proved $D(S)\le -3\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for all $S$, while for finite sets the sharper bound with the constant $2$ is known. We show that the case of infinite sets carries no extra cost: $\textit{any}$ inequality of the form $D(F)\le -α\log R(F)+O(\log\log\frac{1}{R(F)})$ with a computable $α$, valid for all finite $F$, automatically extends to all sets. More generally, we prove a single dichotomy from which such transfer results follow for an arbitrary computable non-decreasing bound, and which also shows that every c.e. set $S$ has a finite subset $F$ such that $F$ has at least as large deterministic complexity as $S$ but randomized one approximately the same or lower. Our result makes qualitative progress on a problem studied by Solovay in 1977 by showing that the search for the optimal constant can be reduced to a purely combinatorial question about a game played with finite sets. In particular, our result yields $D(S)\le-2\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for every $S$, improving Solovay's constant $3$ to $2$.

papers.title: Chiral Majorana hinge modes on a curved surface with magnetic impurities
papers.abstract: Chiral Majorana modes, a key ingredient for topological quantum computation, arise on the surface of a three-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological superconductor when a magnetic field induces a sign-changing surface mass. In practice, the orbital response of the superconductor tilts the surface spectrum and overwhelms the Zeeman term as the field grows. Here we show that magnetic impurities on a spherical surface can instead generate this mass term through their exchange coupling, so that only a weak field is required. The Ising surface Majorana modes mediate a ferromagnetic Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, derived here on the curved surface, that orders the radial impurity moments into an inversion-breaking hedgehog at zero field. An axial field instead stabilizes a domain wall across which the radial magnetization reverses sign, leaving a single chiral Majorana mode along the equator and realizing an inversion-protected second-order topological superconductor.

papers.title: Full-Duplex-Enabled Integrated Sensing and Communications: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is one of the six usage scenarios of IMT-2030, with in-band full duplex (IBFD) being the most direct way to realize it. In this paradigm, a base station that transmits and receives on the same time-frequency resources can sense continuously with its own downlink waveform while serving uplink traffic. This article revisits full-duplex-enabled ISAC (FD-ISAC) in light of the technologies lately shaping sixth-generation (6G) radio design, such as extremely large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems operating in the near field, holographic and dynamic metasurface apertures, fluid and movable antennas, beyond-diagonal reconfigucable intelligent surfaces (BS-RISs) and wave-domain processing with stacked intelligent metasurfaces. We present a holistic FD-ISAC architecture built around a multi-stage, echo-preserving self-interference cancellation chain, and map each 6G technological enabler to the gains it brings and the risks it introduces. A case study with a $28$~GHz full-duplex XL-MIMO base station showcases that near-field-aware beamforming combined with wave-domain, analog, and digital cancellation delivers more than twice the throughput of half-duplex and 3GPP sub-band full-duplex baselines at the same localization-accuracy bound. It is also demonstrated that incorporating a group-connected BD-RIS recovers most of the fully-connected gain at a small fraction of its circuit complexity. The article concludes discussing emerging use cases and open challenges.

papers.title: Perturbation-based Non-perturbative Method
papers.abstract: This paper presents a nonperturbative method for solving eigenproblems. This method applies to almost all potentials and provides nonperturbative approximations for any energy level. The method converts an eigenproblem into a perturbation problem, obtains perturbation solutions through standard perturbation theory, and then analytically continues the perturbative solution into a nonperturbative solution. Concretely, we follow three main steps: (1) Introduce an auxiliary potential that can be solved exactly and treat the potential to be solved as a perturbation on this auxiliary system. (2) Use perturbation theory to obtain an approximate polynomial of the eigenproblem. (3) Use a rational approximation to analytically continue this approximate polynomial into the nonperturbative region.

papers.title: A Tribute to S. Deser: Conserved Quantities in Generic Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: I describe parts of my joint work with S. Deser [March 19, 1931 - April 21, 2023] which started when I was working as a post-doc at Brandeis University in 2001. Our work was mostly, but not exclusively, on conserved charges of higher curvature theories of gravity. I also describe some recent developments, such as expressing the conserved charges in terms of the linearized Riemann tensor; I expound upon the computations. I also reminisce about our interaction for over two decades that went beyond our scientific collaboration. The physics part of this review is intended for graduate students and researchers interested in extended theories of gravity, especially about the conserved quantities and perturbative techniques in these theories.

papers.title: Reciprocity Violation for Mie Scatterers at the Interface and a Scattering Solar Concentrator
papers.abstract: It is shown that reciprocity of the optical path can be violated through asymmetric strength coupling via near-field from resonant Mie scatterers to total internal reflection modes in a dielectric slab. Numerical simulations for silicon nanospheres separated by a nanogap from the glass substrate reveal that at least two orders of magnitude rectification ratio can be realized for such an optical diode configuration. Implementation to a solar light harvesting device, a scattering solar concentrator, is discussed, indicating a similar efficiency is achievable as for the state-of-the-art devices based on luminescence.

papers.title: Affine and cyclic affine equivalence of rotation-symmetric S-boxes
papers.abstract: A rotation-symmetric S-box on $n$ bits is a vectorial Boolean function that commutes with the right cyclic shift and is therefore determined by a single Boolean function. The map $χ$ used in Keccak is a well-known example. Ordinary affine equivalence allows arbitrary invertible affine transformations, which need not preserve rotation symmetry. We introduce \emph{cyclic affine equivalence}, in which the implementing transformations each have an invertible $k$-circulant linear part with $\gcd(k,n)=1$ and a translation vector fixed by the shift. For $n\ge3$, the two relations give the same classes of rotation-symmetric permutations exactly when $n$ is an odd prime for which $2$ is a primitive root. In every other dimension $n\ge3$, explicit constructions exhibit affine classes containing several cyclic affine classes. We derive exact class-size formulas, count cyclic affine classes for $3\le n\le9$, and classify a four-bit family of $χ$-siblings under both relations. Finally, we characterize when a permutation is affinely equivalent to a rotation-symmetric one and apply the criterion to the Ascon S-box.

papers.title: Theory of Berry Singularity Markers: Diagnosing Topological Phase Transitions via Lock-In Tomography
papers.abstract: This work brings forward an alternative approach for inferring the topological character of phase transitions in insulators. The method relies on subjecting the system of interest to a set of external fields which consist of two parts, i.e., a weak spatiotemporally slowly-varying component on top of a constant offset. This process maps the Berry singularities dictating the bulk band structure of the insulator to a synthetic space spanned by the control parameters of the external fields. By measuring the response of the system to the weak part of the perturbations, when these are additionally chosen to form spacetime textures, one can construct a quantity that is here-termed Berry singularity marker (BSM). The BSM enables the Berry singularity detection as it becomes nonzero only in the close vicinity of a Berry singularity and is equal to its charge. Moreover, near the Berry singularities, the BSM encodes the quantum metric tensor of the system. An advantage of the present method is that it can be implemented in a lock-in fashion, thus allowing to ``filter out'' disorder effects, therefore opening the door to the resilient diagnosis of topological phase transitions.

papers.title: Everlasting secure key agreement from a quantum computational hybrid security model
papers.abstract: We introduce the Quantum Computational Timelock (QCT) model, combining time-lock encryption with a quantitative noisy-quantum-storage assumption. Time-lock encryption gives Bob immediate access to the encoding seed and gives Eve the same final information as access to that seed only after a protected interval. Eve may then process her retained information without computational restriction. We state this delayed-access encryption assumption explicitly and construct MUB-QCT from a complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension $d$ and an affine pair-wise independent permutation family. For single-copy encoding, every seed-independent immediate measurement has trace-distance advantage at most $1/(2\sqrt{d+1})$ and mutual information at most $1/(d+1)$. Effective residual storage at diamond distance at most $δ$ from replacement adds at most $δ$ to the individual-attack distinguishing bound. Under i.i.d. individual attacks and entropy-preserving acceptance, we obtain an asymptotic key-rate bound and formulate final-key secrecy in composable trace distance. For $m$ independently randomized signals sharing one bit and seed, the optimal leakage under non-adaptive product measurements is $\min\{1,m/(d+1)\}$, allowing a linear-in-$d$ detection enhancement in that attack model. We also construct a seed-independent joint measurement that recovers the bit after disclosure with error at most $\varepsilon$ from $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ signals, retaining only classical information after measurement. This gives a quantitative separation between product and joint measurements. Bob uses two logical detection outcomes independently of $d$.

papers.title: Quasi-factorization and Multiplicative Comparison of Subalgebra-Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Purely multiplicative comparisons of quantum relative entropy are desirable but challenging to prove. We show such comparisons for relative entropies between comparable densities, including the relative entropy of a density with respect to its subalgebraic restriction. These inequalities are asymptotically tight in approaching known, tight inequalities as perturbation size approaches zero. Based on these results, we obtain a kind of inequality known as quasi-factorization or approximate tensorization of relative entropy. Quasi-factorization lower bounds the sum of a density's relative entropies to several subalgebraic restrictions in terms of its relative entropy to their intersection's subalgebraic restriction. As applications, quasi-factorization implies uncertainty-like relations, and with an iteration trick, it yields decay estimates of optimal asymptotic order on mixing processes described by finite, connected, undirected graphs.

papers.title: A Fresh Look at the Calculation of Tunneling Actions including Gravitational Effects
papers.abstract: Recently, the calculation of tunneling actions, that control the exponential suppression of the decay of metastable vacua, has been reformulated as an elementary variational problem in field space. This paper extends this formalism to include the effect of gravity. Considering tunneling potentials $V_t(φ)$ that go from the false vacuum $φ_+$ to some $φ_0$ on the stable basin of the scalar potential $V(φ)$, the tunneling action is the minimum of the functional $S_E[V_t]=6 π^2m_P^4\int_{φ_+}^{φ_0}(D+V_t')^2/(V_t^2D)dφ$, where $D\equiv [(V_t')^2+6(V-V_t)V_t/m_P^2]^{1/2}$, $V_t'=dV_t/dφ$ and $m_P$ is the reduced Planck mass. This one-line simple result applies equally to AdS, Minkowski or dS vacua decays and reproduces the Hawking-Moss action in the appropriate cases. This formalism provides new handles for the theoretical understanding of different features of vacuum decay in the presence of gravity.

papers.title: Gauge-invariant quantum gravitational corrections to correlation functions
papers.abstract: A recent proposal for gauge-invariant observables in inflation [R. Brunetti et al., JHEP 1608 (2016) 032] is examined. We give a generalisation of their construction to general background spacetimes. In flat space, we calculate one-loop graviton corrections to a scalar two-point function in a general gauge for the graviton. We explicitely show how the gauge-dependent terms cancel between the usual self-energy contributions and the additional corrections inherent in these observables. The one-loop corrections have the expected functional form, contrary to another recently studied proposal for gauge-invariant observables [M. B. Fröb, Class. Quant. Grav. 35 (2018) 035005] where this is not the case. Furthermore, we determine the one-loop graviton corrections to the four-point coupling of the gauge-invariant scalar field, and the corresponding running of the coupling constant induced by graviton loops. Interestingly, the $β$ function is negative for most values of the non-minimal coupling of the scalar field to curvature, including minimal and conformal coupling.

papers.title: Drinfeld J Presentation of Twisted Yangians
papers.abstract: We present a quantization of a Lie coideal structure for twisted half-loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebras. We obtain algebra closure relations of twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for all symmetric pairs of simple Lie algebras and for simple twisted even half-loop Lie algebras. We provide the explicit form of the closure relations for twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for the ${\mathfrak{sl}}_3$ Lie algebra.

papers.title: Equilibria of Replicator Dynamics in Quantum Games
papers.abstract: We analyse two-population replicator dynamics for asymmetric $2\times2$ games implemented with the Marinatto--Weber (MW) identity/bit-flip protocol. The effective payoff matrices are explicit convex combinations of relabelled classical matrices. Consequently, the dynamics depends on the initial state only through its four computational-basis probabilities: quantum phases, coherences and entanglement cannot be distinguished from classical shared randomness by the payoffs or trajectories in this protocol. At each pure-strategy vertex, the local eigenvalues equal the negatives of the corresponding unilateral payoff advantages; a vertex is asymptotically stable precisely when it is a strict Nash equilibrium, and thus an evolutionarily stable strategy pair in the asymmetric-game sense. Explicit examples show how varying the initial distribution changes which vertex is stable. When an isolated interior rest point exists, it is a saddle or a nonlinear centre according to the sign of the product of the classical payoff cross-differences; the sign cannot change under the MW mapping, although the point can enter or leave the strategy square. We give all four vertex-stability conditions explicitly in a single table, obtain a closed-form logistic solution on the parity-balanced hyperplane $S=0$, classify the degenerate cases, and give a first integral for the nondegenerate flow. All results concern the MW payoff protocol and its classically simulable family of bimatrix games; none constitutes evidence of an inherently quantum evolutionary advantage.
